docs.text: The provisional module command python -m rigor_foundry.condition_evaluation_cli --expression expression.json --observations observations.json evaluates the existing condition language over explicit known, absent and unknown observations. It returns distinct true, false and unknown states and never grants effects. See Conditions with partial observations for the exact operand/result versions, input restrictions and exit codes. This separately versioned module command does not change the frozen rigor1.0 inventory.

docs.title: External source provenance
docs.text: source-capture records already-retained HTTPS response bytes under an exact retrieval policy. It does not perform or authorise network access. source-verify deterministically verifies one advisory, version, standard, or content-digest claim against the exact capture and payload. See Verified external source provenance for the complete contract and examples.

docs.title: Offline evidence verification
docs.text:
rigor verify --bundle BUNDLE.json --trust-policy TRUST.json --at TIMESTAMP [--output RESULT.json] verifies signed reports, review attestations, StandardPacks, model-alias collapse, key lifecycle, expiry, and explicit unavailable evidence using only local supplied bytes. The separate trust policy is caller-selected and cannot be replaced from inside the evidence bundle. --at is mandatory UTC so the result is deterministic.

Exit status is zero only when every entry verifies, one for a parseable invalid/stale/unavailable result, and two for malformed or unsafe input. See Offline evidence verification for schemas, signature domains, input restrictions, and the assurance boundary.

docs.title: Explicit adopter bootstrap
docs.text:
rigor bootstrap creates one new trackable policy and one new Git-ignored canonical TODO. It requires explicit --policy, --todo, --review-ledger, --source-root, and --test-root values and never guesses or overwrites them. Parents and source/test roots must already exist without symlink components. The TODO and review-ledger paths must already be ignored; the policy must not be ignored or tracked. Repeat root options for multi-root repositories.

The generated observe-mode policy marks every domain required. Missing portable or native coverage therefore remains visible until the adopter records an evidence-backed applicability decision. See First repository for the complete workflow and failure boundary.

docs.title: Offline CRA preparation
docs.text: cra-bootstrap, vuln-register, vuln-timeline, cra-draft, cra-receipt, cra-skip, user-notice, and cra-status implement the prepare-only CRA reporting workflow. sbom-import and sbom-status add imported-inventory and exact Git-drift evidence. vuln-register accepts a complete content-bound offline OSV adapter bundle as awareness evidence, but still requires separate explicit active-exploitation evidence. The commands retain append-only evidence below .rigor/cra/ and contain no network client. A receipt binds operator-supplied evidence after an external manufacturer action; it does not prove submission or authority acceptance. advisory-draft, advisory-publish, and advisory-delay add append-only fixed-vulnerability advisory evidence without publishing. Publication and delay evidence remains under the repository root because replay binds its relative path and current bytes. cra-pack emits the fixed CRA StandardPack using a caller-supplied Ed25519 signing key; the key is never retained. Policy schema 1.4 explicitly activates CR001–CR006, while schema 1.3 and absent/not-applicable CRA blocks remain inert. See Offline CRA Article 14 preparation for exact commands, deadline semantics, payload partitions, exit codes, and legal-claims boundary. See CRA readiness rules and StandardPack for policy activation, rule verification, pack signing, campaign integration, and the enforcement prohibition.

docs.title: Read-only inspection
docs.text:
rigor scan --root PATH inventories one Git repository and emits candidate evidence. It does not modify the inspected repository.

Git-using commands ignore ambient PATH and accept a shared explicit trust contract: --git-executable, repeatable --git-trust-root, --git-min-version, and --git-max-version-exclusive. An absolute executable requires an explicit containing root. Reports expose the selected Git version, executable digest, and trust-policy digest; JSON reports additionally retain the resolved path, selected root, and provenance identity digest.

JSON report schema 1.3 records git_object_format, the declared ignored-path evidence tuple and digest, and a strict discriminated anchor for every candidate. tracked-blob anchors include path, inclusive line_start/line_end, exact scanned blob_oid, and content_sha256. repository-tree anchors include the path locus, fixed 1:1 state span, tree_oid, and tracked_content_sha256. Markdown output renders the same location, anchor kind, object identity, and digest beside the bounded evidence excerpt.

Ignored evidence is collected only for exact paths declared by policy schema 1.2. JSON never includes ignored file content, link targets, environment values, or recursive directory members. missing and unavailable remain evidence states and do not create findings by themselves.

docs.title: Incremental changed-file view
docs.text: rigor scan --changed-since REF restricts the reported and gated candidates to files changed between the Git revision REF and HEAD. The full deterministic report is still computed (--json-out/--markdown-out write the complete report); --changed-since prints a summary — the number of candidates in changed files, the total, the changed-file count, and the full report digest — followed by those candidates, and makes --fail-on-candidates gate only on the changed set. This lets a pull-request or pre-commit check fail only when the changed code introduces a candidate, without hiding the full-tree report. REF is validated as a plain Git revision (a leading dash can never reach Git as a flag), and the diff runs through the same trusted, provenance-bound Git executable as the scan.

docs.title: SARIF export
docs.text: rigor sarif --report REPORT [--review REVIEWS] [--output RESULTS.sarif] verifies the report and optional review ledger before emitting deterministic SARIF 2.1.0. Without --output, JSON is written to stdout. An explicit output parent must already exist. Export is read-only and includes every candidate; see SARIF export for the state mapping and anchor contract.

docs.title: Content-addressed report differences
docs.text:
rigor report-diff --before BEFORE.json --after AFTER.json [--output DIFF.json] loads and verifies both historical reports, partitions exact candidate identities into retained, appeared, resolved, and anchor-changed classes, and binds the result to both report digests. Missing history fails with status 2; it is never treated as an empty report.

Repository, branch, policy, rule-pack, or scanner changes require the matching --declare-*-change flag and one --justification. Superfluous declarations also fail. Ambiguous relocation can be represented only through a strict --anchor-matches JSON document with exact before/after candidate IDs and a retained rationale. See Content-addressed report differences for the schema, replay contract, and non-verdict boundary.

docs.title: OSCAL export (candidate evidence only)
docs.text: rigor oscal --lock LOCK.json --assessments ASSESSMENTS.json --template TEMPLATE_ID --generated-at TIMESTAMP [--output RESULTS.oscal.json] loads a serialised effective-profile lock and a JSON array of per-control assessments, maps them through a built-in evidence-map template, and emits deterministic OSCAL 1.1.3 assessment-results JSON. The export is triage-only: it is not a certification or attestation, omits findings and risks, requires an explicit UTC --generated-at (no wall clock), and points import-ap at the documented export boundary. Built-in template ids are listed in Compliance evidence maps. Without --output, JSON is written to stdout; an explicit output parent must already exist and the path must be created exclusively.

docs.title: Evidence review
docs.text:
review-template creates explicit review records. validate-review verifies that those records match the exact report. gate and promote reject stale or mismatched state.

When policy declares native adapters, gate requires the explicit --allow-native-audits consent flag. Adapters run in the read-only sandbox and the resulting gate artifact binds HEAD, tree, tracked content, policy, report, executable, command, environment, sandbox, and output digests. Raw argv and output are not retained. The structured sandbox evidence records the complete Bubblewrap compatibility policy, semantic version, binary digest, Debian package version/architecture/status, package-query binary digest, supported option-surface digest, and derived provenance identity. Built-in profiles use the same consent flag and emit structured fail-closed evidence; see Built-in adapter profiles.

docs.title: Rule maturity
docs.text:
rigor maturity-evaluate --cases CASES.json [--output MATURITY.json] reads an explicit schema-1.0 case manifest. Each case names one integrity-verified report file, one review document, an exact candidate identifier, a portable repository identifier, measured reviewer-effort seconds, and one or more retained effort-evidence references. Relative report and review paths resolve from the case-manifest directory. The command selects exactly one completed review per case and rejects stale, incomplete, duplicate, malformed, or digest-changed records.

The manifest policy states minimum review, repository, reviewer, and positive decision counts plus maximum false-positive basis points, median effort, and nearest-rank 90th-percentile effort. It has no implicit default. Output covers the complete built-in rule pack: rules that meet every threshold are active; all others remain probation with finite reason codes. invalid decisions are false positives, while valid and accepted-boundary decisions count as positive adjudications.

rigor gate --mode ratchet and --mode zero require --maturity. The gate also requires repository policy schema 1.3 to bind the maturity report's exact policy_digest as maturity_policy_digest. It binds both the maturity-policy and maturity-report digests, counts active and probationary candidates separately, and lists every probationary rule present in the current report. Probationary candidates cannot block and cannot be omitted from the artifact. Observe mode may run without a maturity report and makes no rule-activation claim. A command-line mode cannot supply an unbound calibration policy while strengthening repository enforcement.

Repository and reviewer identifiers, measured duration, and effort references are operator declarations. Schema validation and content addressing detect unrecomputed changes; they do not authenticate those declarations. Deployments that need authenticated calibration must add signed custody around the case manifest and retained evidence.

docs.title: Independent campaigns
docs.text:
campaign-create, campaign-run, and campaign-compare freeze independent inputs, retain attestations, and record disagreements rather than averaging them away. campaign-create --purpose promotion defaults to two required model witnesses; --required-model-witnesses may raise that threshold.

Campaign schema 1.9 freezes the repository Git object format and ignored inventory in addition to the report input projection. Every campaign-run requires --provider, --model, --model-family, and --operator. The exact identity is content-addressed in the run attestation. Runs from a different object format or ignored state fail as input divergence. Evidence is collected again after native adapters; any mutation rejects the run before attestation.

campaign-run uses the same native consent flag and sandbox boundary. A run without declared native adapters remains passive and does not require consent. Native execution currently requires Debian-family Bubblewrap 0.9.x at /usr/bin/bwrap, with an installed bubblewrap association reported by /usr/bin/dpkg-query. That database association is not a repository-signature or payload-checksum proof; the executable SHA-256 records the actual binary identity. Missing or changed provenance fails closed. Custom Git trust options used for campaign creation must be repeated for every run. A different Git identity is reported as campaign input divergence. campaign-compare accepts the same options for its Git-ignored storage check but does not execute a new repository audit. Runs sharing a model-family value or the same provider/exact-model pair join the same transitive correlation component and count as one witness. Promotion requires an otherwise resolved comparison with at least two witnesses and two declared operator identities. The operator field is auditable protocol evidence, not a cryptographic authentication mechanism. Each witness retains canonical provider/exact-model pairs; comparison loading rejects a family or exact pair repeated across nominally distinct witnesses.

rigor promote requires both --campaign and --comparison. It reloads the durable campaign, runs, reports, and reviews, reconstructs the comparison, and requires the selected report and review to be members of that exact eligible comparison before applying the usual current-tree and explicit-write checks.

docs.title: Classified residual validation
docs.text:
rigor residuals-check --root PATH validates the repository-relative coverage-residuals.json manifest. --manifest selects another repository-relative manifest when a repository adopts the same contract.

The command rejects schema drift, duplicate or unsorted identifiers, source symbol or guard drift, stale symbol digests, missing public verification tests, review dates in the future, expired reviews, and any preregistered negative search match. It does not mark residual lines as covered and does not execute the cited tests; the focused owner tests and remote coverage matrix remain separate required evidence.

Run rigor COMMAND --help for the exact options supported by the installed version.

docs.title: Rule declarations and original components
docs.text: The provisional RuleScope1, SemanticDecision1 and AtomicRule1 records represent exact source-bound declarations. They retain the original ConditionExpression 1.1, SourceSpan1, OwnerProof1 and TypedObjectRef1 contracts. They do not authenticate an issuer, accept semantic extraction or admit a policy for execution.

docs.title: Closed candidate effect catalogues
docs.text:
ExtractorRegistryV3 in rigor_foundry.extractor_registry_v3 declares exactly two fixed extractor contracts: atomic replacement and native profile audit. Its four exact fields are schema_version="3.0", object_kind="extractor-registry", extractors and registry_digest. EffectOperationsV3 in rigor_foundry.effect_operations_v3 binds those descriptors to the actual unchanged EffectVocabularyV2 and EffectTargetTableV2 owners. Its seven fields are schema_version="3.0", object_kind="effect-operations", vocabulary_digest, target_table_digest, extractor_registry_digest, operations and operations_digest. Each owning digest covers every other field, including both common headers.

The public build, from_dict and to_dict boundaries require an explicit PolicyReadBudget1. Use the original bounded policy reader for retained file or byte input. Parsing closes the complete fixed body, descriptor order, nested field types and all dependency identities. Rehashing a changed descriptor does not admit it. Registry allocation counts its two descriptors. Operation allocation counts its three catalogue dependencies, handler/invocation/cancellation contract references, eight total parts and all non-null per-part extractor references (48 references in this fixed version). Final encoded bytes and nesting remain separate limits. Serializers revalidate direct instances and return fresh maps.

Inline input_contract and output_contract values are closed mappings of owning type names and required checks. They are digest-covered payloads without separate identity or typed-reference formats. The invocation contract digest hashes the corresponding complete input mapping. Cancellation contract preimages name the exact operation and its required authority/cancellation boundaries; the native requirement includes durable stage journaling, separately authorised owned-child cleanup, retained custody on denied cleanup and no automatic replay. These are candidate requirements for an installed consumer to implement and qualify. Metadata parsing neither provides that consumer nor implements the declared NativeOperationBindingV3 or ExtractedPartV3 owners.

The atomic descriptor retains its original immutable invocation and one filesystem part. Native templates retain all seven parts in fixed order: repository read, workspace-parent write, owned-child cleanup, Git execution, version execution, sandbox execution and audit execution. Shared original execute actions do not remove template parts. Compute parts use the original compute-job/compute-host classification; an installed extractor must still bind separate actual executable and allocation rights. A descriptor never authorises deleting its parent or sibling, enrolling a host, importing an arbitrary module or launching a command. Full selected source/semantic acceptance, actual extraction, held root/gate leases and durable effect dispatch remain required before execution. Original v2 parsing and consumers remain separate.

Every parser and serializer requires an explicit PolicyReadBudget1. Document bytes and container nesting are checked before child parsing; collection owners also enforce source and aggregate reference limits. Inputs with unknown fields, unsupported versions, reordered sets, duplicate identities, invalid UTF-8 or incorrect digests refuse. For file input, use read_policy_document from rigor_foundry.policy_source_reads before the record's from_dict method. That reader also rejects duplicate JSON keys and uses bounded stable file reads.

docs.title: Typed v3 signatures
docs.text:
TrustRolesV3 in rigor_foundry.rule_chain_trust_v3 binds five exact original OfflineTrustPolicy objects. Original lifecycle validation enforces distinct key identifiers and public keys across roles, v1 nonsemantic keys, and v2 semantic keys with disjoint enrolled author/reviewer identities. Its trust_roles_digest is the canonical digest of schema_version="3.0" and the five named original policy digests: pack_issuers, project_selectors, lock_resolvers, semantic_authors, and semantic_reviewers. Any change to any selected policy changes this generation identity, including an unrelated role's rotation or revocation metadata.

rule_chain_v3_signature_boundary resolves the closed kind/body-version/role/ domain table. RuleChainV3Signature, in rigor_foundry.signed_rule_chain_v3, parses exactly twelve fields and requires an explicit read budget. Its payload binds signature schema, kind, body schema, domain, canonical body digest and UTC signing time; its signature digest hashes actual Ed25519 bytes.

The factory normalizes accepted UTC timestamp spellings with the original timestamp owner before storing them or deriving the signed payload. Serialized records use that canonical spelling ending in Z. Direct records and wire objects carrying a noncanonical alias refuse instead of emitting a record that cannot roundtrip. Normalizing a factory input preserves its actual payload and signature bytes.

Signature kind Body version Role Domain standard-pack 3.0 pack-issuer rigor-foundry.standard-pack.v3 project-profile 3.0 project-selector rigor-foundry.project-profile-selection.v3 effective-profile-lock 3.0 lock-resolver rigor-foundry.effective-profile-lock.v3 rule-corpus-author 1.0 semantic-author rigor-foundry.rule-corpus-author.v3 rule-corpus-acceptance 1.0 semantic-reviewer rigor-foundry.rule-corpus-acceptance.v3

verify requires the consuming owner's independently expected kind, body version/digest, selected whole-policy digest, current UTC instant and complete policies. It reparses metadata and every original policy, then verifies the actual signature and key activity both at signing and now. Future timestamps, expired/revoked/unknown keys, changed role policies and cross-version replay refuse. Both corpus roles sign the same acceptance body under distinct domains.

This is a signature primitive over an already validated body digest. The consuming body owner must separately parse its complete actual pack, profile, lock or corpus-acceptance body and establish its trusted source. This API does not itself parse or admit those bodies, ratify semantics, enroll keys, select a host or grant effects. Original v2 signatures retain their original grammar and domains; the new provisional modules do not change the stable1.0 surface.

docs.title: Scope and exact statements
docs.text:
A global scope has no condition and explicitly lists every supported task event. A scoped rule has an original condition and a nonempty sorted event subset. Missing facts remain unknown under evaluate_condition_state; structural scope parsing does not authenticate fact producers or decide a gate.

from rigor_foundry.policy_read_budget import PolicyReadBudget1
from rigor_foundry.rule_scope import RuleScope1
from rigor_foundry.task_context import TASK_CONTEXT_EVENTS

limits = PolicyReadBudget1.build(
    max_document_bytes=65536,
    max_source_bytes=65536,
    max_total_source_bytes=131072,
    max_sources=16,
    max_rules=64,
    max_references=1024,
    max_depth=32,
)
scope = RuleScope1.build(
    scope_kind="global",
    condition=None,
    events=tuple(sorted(TASK_CONTEXT_EVENTS)),
    budget=limits,
)
assert RuleScope1.from_dict(scope.to_dict(budget=limits), budget=limits) == scope

AtomicRule1 hashes the statement's exact UTF-8 bytes, including whitespace and original newline characters. Source spans retain their declared selection order. Dependencies and decision IDs are sorted unique sets; a rule cannot depend on itself. Component references sort by (kind, format_version, object_id) and cannot give two digests to one identity. Proposed, active, held, superseded and retired declarations remain explicit. An active lifecycle string is not semantic acceptance.

SemanticDecision1 retains the issuer, original spans, rationale, condition, affected rules, successors and original owner proof. Its relations are supersedes, exception, exclusion, interpretation and adoption. Supersession has nonempty distinct directed rule sets. Complete graph resolution, competent issuer authentication and exception permission remain required at the consuming boundary; dates, filenames and matching hashes establish none of these.

docs.title: Original component resolution
docs.text:
PolicyComponent1 and resolve_policy_component, from rigor_foundry.source_component_reader, resolve these actual original owners:

Reference kind Format Original model Owning digest control-definition 1.0 ControlDefinition control_digest evidence-contract 1.0 EvidenceContract contract_digest evidence-reference 1.0 reference binding EvidenceReference evidence_digest review-attestation 2.0 ReviewerAttestation attestation_digest authority-clause 2.0 AuthorityClauseV2 clause_digest freshness-policy 2.0 FreshnessPolicyV2 policy_digest adapter-lock 1.0 reference binding AdapterLock adapter_digest reviewer-identity-policy semantic-reviewer-identity-policy.v1 ReviewerIdentityPolicy policy_digest

The original complete serialized objects are unchanged. The control identity is its original versioned_id; the numeric evidence contract uses contract_id. Authority and freshness use clause_id and policy_id. No object_kind is inserted into these legacy objects. The adapter uses its original adapter_id and all eight original fields, including its tool version. Its reference format 1.0 identifies this fixed binding; it adds no version header to the adapter itself. Unknown adapter fields refuse before the original parser. The identity policy has no original object ID; both reference ID and digest use its complete original policy_digest. Its trust policy, key lifecycles and reviewer bindings remain unchanged. Original evidence references have exactly eleven fields and no schema header. Their fixed reader closes those fields before the unchanged original parser; reference format 1.0 does not add a header. Original review attestations retain all thirteen fields, schema 2.0 and the signature domain rigor-foundry.reviewer-attestation.v1. Their complete attestation digest is their reference ID; the separate signed reviewer identity may contain spaces. Original control applicability, numeric freshness, independent reviewer count and remediation obligations remain intact. A reference cannot appoint a loader or turn a source metadata object into an enforcement component.

Resolution validates the complete supplied component cohort, including unselected members, under count and aggregate byte limits. Missing targets, duplicate identities, altered original digests and normalization of legacy input refuse. Resolving a component establishes its structural identity, rather than its signatures, current selection or accepted relation to an atomic rule.

docs.title: Explicit review and evidence contracts
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.review_policy provides provisional ReviewRoleRequirement1 and ReviewPolicy1 records at version 1.0. Each role binds an exact original reviewer identity policy and an explicit independence requirement. A review policy retains its mode (independent, self-review or conditional-self-review), sorted unique roles, source rule IDs and named unavailability fact references. Parsing these declarations does not appoint reviewers or establish that a manager is unavailable. Empty declarations grant no fallback or approval. A consuming assessment must verify actual role eligibility, source permission and authenticated unavailability before allowing conditional SelfReview.

rigor_foundry.evidence_contract_v2 provides EvidenceRequirement1 at 1.0 and EvidenceContract2 at 2.0. Each requirement retains an evidence type, exact adapter reference, subject class and exact original freshness-policy reference. A contract requires a nonempty sorted unique requirement set and an explicit review-policy reference. Aggregate reference limits apply before child parsing. The contract does not invent numeric freshness or reviewer counts; legacy EvidenceContract records keep their original positive TTL, adapter and evidence sets, and minimum independent reviewer count.

The new review and evidence records expose build, to_dict and from_dict with an explicit read budget. ReviewPolicy1.reference and EvidenceContract2.reference bind their complete owning digests. Resolve their targets through the corresponding new owning parser; the original context-source resolver does not acquire these formats merely because a typed reference parses.

docs.title: Rule-bound qualitative controls
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.control_definition_v2.ControlDefinition2 is provisional at 2.0. It binds an explicit rule ID, original scope, require/deny mode, qualitative evidence contract and unchanged original remediation contract. Domain, severity and target maturity retain their existing vocabularies. It has no implicit default applicability or separate legacy condition field.

control.verify_rule_binding(rule, budget=limits) accepts an actual AtomicRule1 and rechecks both complete records. Rule ID, mode and complete scope must agree, and the rule must contain the exact control reference, including its owning digest. The new boundary also closes the original remediation's seven fields while preserving its exact text, order and obligations. Original ControlDefinition 1.0 serialization remains unchanged.

Atomic enforcement references allow original control 1.0, authority 2.0 and freshness 2.0, together with qualitative control 2.0 and review-policy 1.0. Bare adapters and reviewer identity policies are support dependencies; they cannot become atomic enforcement components. Structural control binding does not establish source acceptance, applicability, evidence validity or a gate verdict.

docs.title: Original signed-pack bindings
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.component_source_resolution.parse_policy_component_target resolves fourteen closed policy target formats: the eight original component formats listed above; new ControlDefinition2, EvidenceContract2, ReviewPolicy1, EvidenceReference2 and SemanticDecision1; and original StandardPackV2 at 2.0. Each fixed branch compares the complete actual target reference, including its original ID and owning digest. Unsupported pairs refuse before target parsing; the context-source resolver keeps its separate supported subset.

StandardPackSource2 bounds the complete original pack before its existing recursive serializer/parser runs. It requires actual original child types and immutable collections for direct instances, and exact arrays for wire input. Control counts and aggregate references include every control, condition, authority grantor and freshness invalidator. All original controls, child wires and detached signature bytes remain present. Its reference uses original pack_id and complete pack_digest; the original pack version remains inside that digest. Reading a pack does not verify current trust or semantic acceptance.

rigor_foundry.legacy_control_binding.LegacyControlBinding1 is provisional at 1.0. It binds a source rule to an exact original control 1.0 within an original signed pack 2.0, together with sorted unique source decision IDs. binding.verify_pack(pack, budget=limits) revalidates the complete actual pack and returns its exact matching original control. Empty packs, absent controls, different owning digests and qualitative-control casts refuse. Original target maturity, applicability condition/default, numeric freshness, reviewer count, adapter/evidence requirements and remediation remain intact. This membership check does not establish complete selected-control enumeration or permission for an exception, waiver or gate approval.

docs.title: Qualitative freshness declarations
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.freshness_proof provides provisional InvalidatorObservation1 and FreshnessProof1 at 1.0. An invalidator retains clear, invalid or unknown explicitly. clear requires an original OwnerProof1; a parsed proof envelope still needs authentication by its installed current owner.

A freshness proof binds the exact original freshness-policy reference, mode, independent subject digest, original subject proof, sorted unique invalidator observations and subject snapshot. Its subject proof must match that digest and snapshot. Invalidator owners retain their own source snapshots. No duration, expiry or observation timestamp is inferred. Explicit legacy expiry and key or grant lifecycle rules remain separate.

proof.verify_policy_binding(policy, budget=limits) requires an actual original FreshnessPolicyV2 and compares its complete identity, mode and invalidator set. This checks structural binding. Invalid and unknown observations remain present; the method does not authenticate clear or return a freshness verdict. For every invalidator, the installed verifier must resolve its actual selected owner, source contract and independent current observation, then establish that the ID/state governs this outer subject and its relevant state or generation. Missing, unrelated, contradictory, stale, revoked or unauthenticated observations cannot establish clear; invalid and unknown cannot pass. Held source checks remain required through use and closure.

The invalidator record's observation_digest includes its proof envelope. The original owner's observation_digest hashes its independently observed ContextProducerObservation1 preimage. These digests are distinct; equating them would introduce a circular proof. freshness_reference_count(value, budget=limits) lets enclosing consumers bound the complete nested allocation before parsing children. It counts the policy, subject-proof pair, invalidator IDs and optional original proof pairs.

docs.title: Independent evidence subjects
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.evidence_reference_v2.evidence_subject_digest derives the closed evidence-subject 1.0 identity before either included proof exists. It hashes the exact adapter reference, artifact digest and byte count, configuration, toolchain, cohort and complete sorted unique source-object references. No producer proof, freshness proof or enclosing evidence digest enters this subject.

Provisional EvidenceReference2 at 2.0 adds the evidence identity/type, classification, opaque reference, validated UTC observation time, declared result, original producer proof and qualitative freshness proof. Both included proof subjects must match the independently computed evidence subject. Producer and freshness owners may retain different source snapshots. Changed artifact, source, configuration, toolchain or cohort identities cannot retain the old proof binding. All nested reference allocations and source counts respect the explicit budget.

Results pass, fail, unavailable and refused remain declarations until the installed adapter parses the actual retained artifact and current owners verify its complete scope and proofs. Neither result text nor structural parsing grants approval. The opaque reference field embeds no raw artifact or credentials and does not grant permission to read a path or URL. object_reference(budget=limits) returns its exact typed evidence identity, separately from that artifact reference.

evidence.verify_requirement_binding(requirement, policy, budget=limits) checks the actual EvidenceRequirement1, adapter, evidence type, subject class and original freshness policy. It supplies no assessment verdict. The original numeric EvidenceReference keeps its exact separate wire and expiry semantics; neither parser migrates the other format.

docs.title: Shared original assessment predicates
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.assessment_evidence_validation factors the existing legacy predicates into three functions. They consume original validated contract, adapter, evidence, attestation and trust-store inputs; they create no profile or lock and grant no source selection or operational authority.

  • validate_original_evidence_bindings requires one exact original adapter identity and owning digest for each reference, covering the control domain.
  • validate_original_pass_evidence retains the original positive numeric age bound, explicit expiry, nonempty evidence and complete required adapter/type coverage. Every submitted item must be fresh; a fresh member cannot hide another expired or future observation.
  • validate_original_reviewers retains actual Ed25519 verification of the exact original assessment body and decision, current review interval, explicit trust store and required distinct reviewer IDs, key IDs and public keys. The original case-sensitive identity comparison remains unchanged.

The existing public ControlAssessment now calls these same predicates. Its wire 1.1, original review-body identity, status/applicability, waiver and limitations rules remain unchanged. New selected consumers must supply their own actual selected source/control relations and independently derived review body; these functions do not appoint owners or infer SelfReview permission.

docs.title: Complete quality projection
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.quality_projection_v3.QualityProjectionRowV3 retains an exact control reference, source rule IDs, scope, evidence contract, reviewer policy, target maturity and applicability decision references. Its format is 3.0.

The legacy1 case binds the actual original control and numeric evidence contract at 1.0. It preserves the original Boolean default_applicable, nullable original condition and target maturity; review_policy is null because the original positive reviewer count remains in the evidence contract. The qualitative2 case binds the actual qualitative control and evidence contract at 2.0, with its explicit review-policy reference. Its default and condition are null because its RuleScope1 owns applicability.

row.verify_control_binding(control, budget=limits) reparses the actual complete owning control and compares every projected obligation. Qualitative rows also retain the control's exact scope and source rule relation. Rehashing a row cannot repair a different control digest, evidence contract, review policy, maturity or original applicability field.

validate_quality_projection(rows, controls, budget=limits) requires exactly one complete row per supplied selected control, sorted by its exact versioned identity. It validates both actual control generations and the complete cohort, including aggregate reference counts and encoded array bytes. Missing, extra, duplicate or reordered rows refuse. The enclosing owner must derive the supplied controls from its actual selected signed generation; this structural check does not establish selection or evaluate applicability.

Applicability decisions use exact SemanticDecision1 references at 1.0. decision.reference(budget=limits) binds the complete declaration's original ID and digest; the fixed policy target resolver reparses its actual owner. Issuer authentication, source acceptance and permission for exceptions remain separate required checks. None of these APIs supplies a gate verdict.

docs.title: Selected assessment inputs
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.selected_control_assessment_v2.SelectedControlAssessment2 uses the exact 2.0 wire. It binds the selected lock, quality projection, task and event request digests; the actual control generation; explicit applicability and status; evidence and review references; assessor, timestamp and reason. legacy1 references original evidence at reference format 1.0; qualitative2 references EvidenceReference2. Both retain the actual original signed review attestation format 2.0. Reference identities are sorted and unique under complete byte and allocation bounds.

Applicability is the string true, false or unknown, separately from any legacy Boolean default. Unknown cannot pass, and false remains explicitly unassessed. A declared status, including pass or accepted-risk, supplies no authentication or gate result. Current contract, evidence, reviewer and exact source exception verification remain the installed consumer's responsibility; accepted risk cannot replace a mandatory source floor's pass.

assessment.verify_quality_binding(row, control, budget=limits) verifies the actual complete quality row and owning control generation. The enclosing owner must independently derive the complete selected cohort and verify the lock, projection, task and request identities; coordinated subsets of the row/control inputs cannot prove that completeness.

assessment.review_body_digest(budget=limits) hashes every assessment field except reviews and the final assessment_digest. Reviews can therefore sign the independent complete input before their references are added. Changing a lock, projection, task or request changes that body; adding the resulting review references changes the final assessment digest without changing its review body. Original Ed25519 attestations keep their original signature domain, exact body binding and validity checks. A digest or parsed signature alone authenticates neither a reviewer nor a selected generation.

validate_selected_legacy_pass consumes the exact selected assessment, quality row and original control alongside complete original adapter, evidence and attestation cohorts, an explicit original public trust store and an aware evaluation instant. It revalidates all complete owners, matches the declared evidence/review references and applies the same original numeric freshness, adapter/type coverage and positive independent reviewer predicates used by ControlAssessment. Actual original Ed25519 signatures bind its independently derived review body. Missing trust, self review, insufficient distinct quorum, stale/future/expired evidence and changed request bodies refuse. No v1 lock is created. Complete selected-root/source custody, artifact/result observation, key lifecycle and closing verification still belong to the installed consumer.

Supporting evidence contracts, evidence references, reviewer identity policies, attestations, adapter custody and semantic decisions cannot become atomic enforcement components merely because their fixed target readers exist.

docs.title: Complete declared rule graphs
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.source_semantic_graph.source_rule_dependency_order revalidates the complete sorted rule and semantic-decision cohorts. It resolves every declared dependency, decision and affected/successor target, including held and historical rows. A rule's decision reference must actually name that rule in the decision's affected or successor set. Endpoints are checked even when the rule has no redundant backlink; an empty source-only decision creates no rule.

The complete declared dependency relation and the complete declared supersedes relation must both be acyclic. Conditional decisions and inactive lifecycle labels cannot hide a declared supersession cycle. Interpretation, adoption and exclusion metadata do not become supersession edges. Directed set expansion has an allocation bound before any Cartesian edge set is materialized.

The returned IDs contain every supplied rule exactly once, after its dependencies. Simultaneously available nodes sort by exact ID; this ordering does not select semantic precedence. Complete encoded metadata bytes, source counts and declared reference allocations are bounded across both cohorts.

The installed owner must still authenticate the actual complete source cohort, issuer competence, scope and current condition facts; independently derive all effective decisions; check simultaneous conflicts and prove exception authority. Caller-selected omissions or a successful graph traversal establish none of those requirements and grant no gate result.

The retained source universe separately verifies the complete host-selected original source cohort and byte partitions. Neither that byte accounting nor these declaration records establish semantic completeness. Source access, issuer decisions, corpus acceptance, current host selection and permission for effects remain separate owning checks.

docs.title: Deterministic source document inputs
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.rule_source_document.RuleSourceDocument1 retains the complete source universe, original byte regions, atomic rules, semantic decisions, qualitative controls, review policies, legacy control bindings, original freshness policies and authority references. Each collection has a fixed child owner; extra fields, duplicate identities, mutable direct collections and changed child digests refuse. Original children keep their complete original wire.

Collections sort by their exact identities. Regions retain (source_id, start_byte) order. Legacy bindings use the composite (rule_id, pack.object_id, control.object_id): a rule may bind multiple original controls and an original control may have several source rules. Repeated triples refuse even when their binding digests differ. Digest ordering never selects a different convention.

Explicit aggregate reference, byte, collection and nesting limits cover the whole document, including its envelope and final digest. Original region links, source counts and freshness invalidators are bounded before their original child parsers allocate the corresponding records. The separate compiler_contract_digest identifies the compiler contract input. Serialization adds no timestamp, resulting pack/profile/lock, signature or corpus acceptance. The document digest hashes every other complete listed field deterministically.

from_dict checks bounded structural integrity; it does not resolve external typed targets, accept source extraction or authenticate semantic decisions. The consuming compiler must still verify the complete original source cohort, same retained bytes and region/span joins, all component and decision relations, original pack membership and actual source/issuer/corpus acceptance. A structurally valid document supplies none of those permissions by itself.

docs.title: Source compilation with retained owners
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.rule_source_compiler.compile_rule_source_document takes the existing SourceUniverseOwner and complete explicit rule, region, decision and component cohorts. It obtains the universe from that actual owner. There is no caller-supplied replacement universe, filesystem discovery or prose interpreter. Repeated compilation of the same complete inputs and held owner state is identical; the compiler adds no timestamp or resulting selection.

rule_source_compiler_contract_digest() separately identifies the document schema, fixed target table, composite legacy order, complete declared graph, component joins and retained source checks. This contract identity is separate from the document digest, actual implementation custody and semantic acceptance.

verify_rule_source_document revalidates the complete document and returns all rule IDs in dependency-first order. It verifies the actual complete source cohort initially, resolves every supplied external component through its fixed owning parser, and rejects inconsistent versioned target identities even in unused support objects. Whole target bytes and typed-reference counts are bounded together with the document. Original pack members and their nested numeric evidence contracts keep their actual original identities.

Every rule component must be declared by the complete emitted cohort, and every emitted component has an owning rule. Active rules require enforcement components and a declared normative source region. Qualitative controls retain exact rule/scope/mode bindings; their evidence references resolve the actual inline review/freshness policies, exact adapter and matching subject class. Review policy source-rule IDs equal the rules that actually reference it. Required reviewer identity policies resolve as complete original objects.

Legacy bindings verify the exact original pack member. All controls, authority clauses and freshness policies of each referenced original pack remain accounted for; a valid pack signature cannot excuse a dropped control. Signature bytes, old numeric evidence and original conditions are preserved. Parsing these records does not authenticate current signing trust or transition scope.

Source/region/rule/decision links resolve in both directions. Every citation has an overlapping declared same-source region, and every region's declared rule/decision has a matching citation. Half-open byte intervals do not overlap at adjacent endpoints. Lookup uses indexed source relations and sorted interval indexes without rewriting the retained citation order. Duplicate span IDs must refer to identical complete spans. Rule output classification cannot be less restricted than its cited source.

The same actual source owner finally verifies complete byte partitions and original span bytes, including closing source and implementation checks. Held or excluded sources cannot supply included citations. A source-only exclusion can retain an explicit exclusion decision without inventing a rule endpoint; that declaration still needs actual competent issuer and corpus acceptance.

The result remains a compiled source candidate. Declared byte overlap does not prove adequacy of the extracted prose. Competent issuer/effective decision verification, independent corpus/native ratification, current root selection, evidence authentication, gate evaluation and effect authority remain separate required owning boundaries.

docs.title: Complete corpus acceptance
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.rule_corpus_acceptance.rule_corpus_acceptance_body derives the common unsigned body from the entire actual RuleSourceDocument1 and an exact RuleCorpusRatification1. Its nine fields include both headers, corpus ID, document, universe, decision, component and compiler digests, and the native ratification reference. Universe and decision digests hash their complete wire arrays. The component digest hashes the complete five-key mapping containing qualitative_controls, review_policies, legacy_control_bindings, authority_bindings and freshness_policies, including empty arrays.

RuleCorpusAcceptance1 adds the full author and reviewer signatures and its final digest, giving exactly twelve fields at schema 1.0. Both signatures bind the same unsigned body under their separate v3 domains. Parsing validates their complete metadata, kind, body version and body identity. Current crypto, key lifecycle and protected policy selection remain consuming checks, so an old envelope remains structurally readable without becoming currently valid.

rigor_foundry.rule_corpus_ratification.RuleCorpusRatification1 retains exactly eleven fields at 1.0: both headers, corpus/document/universe/decision identities, issuer ID, original native-pin reference, original statement span, statement digest and final ratification digest. Its reference and span must name the same original source. The record contains neither a host provider nor an issuer-enrollment instruction.

docs.title: Exact native corpus statement
docs.text:
render_rule_corpus_question, in rigor_foundry.rule_corpus_native, renders the entire actual document as JSON with sorted keys, compact separators, unescaped Unicode and no nonfinite values. Fixed surrounding prose requests this exact decoded user text:

SCHVAĽUJEM rule-corpus <corpus_id> <document_digest> <universe_digest> <decision_set_digest>

The rendered question and expected user text have no terminal LF. Original native capture processing appends exactly one LF to each decoded message. A user-authored terminal LF therefore produces two capture LFs and refuses the exact statement grammar. No stripping, whitespace normalization, NFC conversion or abbreviated document is accepted. The complete rendering, including the capture owner's LF, must fit the explicit document budget.

RuleCorpusNativeOwner borrows actual RetainedContextSource pin metadata, the entire RetainedPolicySource JSONL and an already-held original HostNativeSourceState. Installed composition separately supplies the competent issuer, exact corpus scope and protected expected issuer-binding digest. rule_corpus_native_binding_digest hashes the fixed rigor-foundry.rule-corpus-native-issuer-binding.v1 contract identifier, those two IDs and the complete original native reference. Computing this digest does not authenticate its selection; it must match independently installed state.

Verification joins the complete question, exact decoded statement, original selected user role/message/line identity, later reply timestamp, full file hash/path, captures, current selected pin and revocations. The statement span covers the entire original selected user JSONL line, including carrier LF; bounded scanning derives its exact offsets from that same retained file. Three SHA-256 preimages stay distinct: decoded statement UTF-8; the same text plus one capture LF; and the whole original JSONL line. Escaped Unicode in the carrier does not change the decoded statement or permit a plaintext span. Closing rechecks the whole borrowed snapshot without closing its owning leases.

docs.title: Held corpus verification
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.rule_corpus_verification.RuleCorpusVerifier.verified_context composes the actual source/compiler, native and selected-signature owners. It compares the complete accepted unsigned body with the actual document and ratification, verifies both real signatures against the whole selected policy generation and current installed clock, and runs the complete original source compiler and target checks. Included unread, unavailable or protected sources prevent acceptance readiness. An unresolved source region also retains its hold before consumer use and during closing checks, even when both signatures and the complete native approval bind that exact disposition. Structural document and envelope parsing and the declaration-only compiler preserve the unresolved region; its bytes and rule/decision relations remain present.

The native approval carrier must remain outside the complete corpus inputs. The source owner checks original retained paths and declared payload digests, including held metadata, rather than trusting a copied universe. Appending an approval to a transcript already hashed inside its own document changes that input and cannot ratify the unchanged document.

All checks repeat on context closure, including current time, native revocations and retained source identities; a changed accepted generation refuses. The installed outer host holds the original leases and state through use and close. Where original native source selection obtains a context internally, its adapter must borrow that already-held state without acquiring another producer generation. Caller-created owners, hashes or role markers install no authority.

These provisional module APIs verify an exact source extraction cohort under their installed composition. Effective semantic precedence, exception authority, current applicability, enclosing pack/profile/lock selection, evidence, common gate verdicts and effect permission still require their own actual owners.

docs.title: Explicit policy hold declarations
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.policy_hold.PolicyHold1 retains exactly seven fields at 1.0: the common schema and kind, an authored reason code, an exact typed subject, affected_rule_ids, evidence and hold_digest. The digest covers every other field, including both headers and complete child-reference digests.

Rule IDs form a sorted unique set; supporting references sort uniquely by (kind, format_version, object_id). Two references to the same typed identity with different digests refuse. Empty rule or evidence arrays remain explicit. The subject, every rule and every evidence reference share one aggregate reference budget. Separate rule, complete encoded byte and nesting bounds apply before wire children are parsed. Direct records also require immutable collections and actual revalidated original reference objects.

For a file, use read_policy_document before PolicyHold1.from_dict, with the same explicit PolicyReadBudget1. The original bounded reader rejects duplicate keys; the record rejects missing, additional, wrong-version and malformed fields. References retain their existing closed target formats and never select loaders.

This provisional declaration neither resolves its referenced targets nor authenticates the reason, affected rules or evidence. The enclosing selected policy owner must derive and verify the complete current hold cohort. Parsing, omitting or editing a record cannot clear a hold, admit a policy or grant effects.

docs.title: Complete signed pack and profile source bindings
docs.text:
StandardPackV3, from rigor_foundry.rule_chain_pack_v3, uses an exact thirteen-field parent3 envelope. Its controls use ControlDefinition2 and its authority and freshness children keep their unchanged original formats. The canonical source-document digest and complete corpus-acceptance digest are separate fields. The source URI is nonblank, whitespace-free opaque descriptive metadata; parsing preserves it exactly and never fetches it. At least one actual component is required, and the complete parent and nested references must fit the explicit processing budget. Component identities retain their kind and the control's exact version; distinct versions or kinds can share an identifier, while duplicate typed identities refuse. body returns the exact unsigned signing preimage. build and from_dict validate complete signature metadata and the enclosing digest; actual crypto and source admission require the consuming owner.

PackSelectionV3, ProfileRuleDisposition1 and ProjectProfileV3, from rigor_foundry.rule_chain_profile_v3, retain explicit selected-pack order. Pack IDs are unique. An original2 pack selection has an exact transition digest and null corpus field. A new3 selection has the exact corpus digest and null transition field. The enclosing profile independently binds the complete corpus in both cases; original null metadata creates no legacy exemption. Every declared mandatory rule has an included disposition. Exclusions carry an exact decision identity; parsing does not accept that decision's authority. The complete actual source cohort, rather than a caller's signed subset, determines which rules and components must be present.

ProfileSourceVerifierV3.verified_context, from rigor_foundry.profile_source_verification, borrows the actual held RuleCorpusVerifier and already-held original HostPackSourceState objects. The installed composition independently selects the expected profile digest, project and scope. Pure original pack-source verifiers borrow those states; this API never enters another legacy selected-chain provider. Original2 signatures retain their original domain and lifecycle owners. New pack and profile signatures use their exact3 domains and the whole selected trust-policy generation, with the same installed current clock. The entire selected pack-body cohort has aggregate byte and nested-reference limits. Original retained source reads also enforce source count, individual payload and complete payload limits.

Within the actual complete corpus context, the owner compares every ordered pack selection to the real owning body and verifies all selected source bytes and signatures. It independently joins all qualitative and original numeric controls, original pack bindings, authority clauses, freshness policies, source-rule dispositions and declared mandatory identities. A legacy fact-context reference is required exactly when selected original conditions need it; this checks the declaration relation, while current fact authentication belongs to the effective-root owner. Omitted, replaced, duplicated or unrelated components refuse, including coordinated freshly signed subsets. Source relations, current signatures and proof generation are checked again at closure; the outer corpus repeats original source/native checks too. Consumer exceptions propagate.

The yielded ProfileSourceBindingsV3 is read-only Python source evidence valid inside that context. It is not an effective lock or permission. Original transition/native semantics, competent exclusion and precedence decisions, current fact ownership and applicability, effective root resolution, evidence assessment and effect rights still require their separate actual owning checks. These APIs remain provisional module surfaces; original pack/profile parsers, stable package exports and CLI contracts keep their existing interpretations.

docs.title: Compliance evidence maps and OSCAL export
docs.text: RigorFoundry can relate its per-control audit evidence to named external control standards and export the result as OSCAL assessment results. These surfaces are for triage and reporting only. They are not a certification, an attestation, or a claim of compliance with any standard.

docs.title: What a template is
docs.text:
An evidence-map template names one external standard and maps every RigorFoundry audit domain to that standard's control identifiers, or declares an explicit gap where no relevant control exists. A silent gap is never permitted: every domain carries an explicit decision.

Each mapping records an honest relation strength:

  • supporting — the domain evidence directly supports the control objective;
  • partial — the evidence supports one aspect of the control;
  • context — the evidence is contextual input only.

Templates reference external control identifiers (for example A.8.28 or CC7.1) and name each standard's edition and licence. They never reproduce copyrighted control text.

docs.title: Built-in templates
docs.text:
Template id Standard Edition (verified at source) iso-iec-27001-2022 ISO/IEC 27001 information security management systems 2022, including Amendment 1:2024 (iso.org) aicpa-tsc-2017 AICPA Trust Services Criteria 2017 with revised points of focus, 2022 (aicpa-cima.com) eu-cra-2024-2847 Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 CRA evidence crosswalk Official Journal text, 20 November 2024 (EUR-Lex) 
from rigor_foundry.compliance_maps import builtin_template, builtin_template_ids

print(builtin_template_ids())            # includes 'eu-cra-2024-2847'
template = builtin_template("iso-iec-27001-2022")
mapping = template.mapping_for("application-security")
print([reference.reference for reference in mapping.references])

Every template and standard descriptor is content-addressed with a SHA-256 digest and validates its own integrity on parse.

docs.title: Export boundary
docs.text:
report_oscal renders deterministic OSCAL 1.1.3 assessment-results JSON from an effective profile lock, its per-control assessments, and one template. The export is a boundary, not an attestation:

  • each assessment becomes one OSCAL observation with the RigorFoundry status, domain, and assessment digest, plus one related-control property for every mapped external control identifier;
  • findings and risks are omitted — RigorFoundry emits candidate observations, not attested findings or residual risk;
  • import-ap references this documented boundary, not an authored OSCAL assessment plan;
  • the metadata carries the non-certification notice and names every unsupported field explicitly.

Object identifiers are deterministic (RFC-4122 name-based UUIDs derived from the input digests), so the same inputs always produce byte-identical output. A generated_at UTC timestamp is required; the export never reads a wall clock.

from rigor_foundry.compliance_maps import builtin_template
from rigor_foundry.oscal_export import export_digest, report_oscal

template = builtin_template("aicpa-tsc-2017")
document = report_oscal(lock, assessments, template, "2026-07-15T12:00:00Z")
digest = export_digest(lock, assessments, template, "2026-07-15T12:00:00Z")

The mapped standards remain the property of their publishers; RigorFoundry references identifiers and editions only.

docs.title: Conditions with partial observations
docs.text:
The provisional Python evaluator distinguishes an observed value, declared absence and missing knowledge. It consumes the existing ConditionExpression schema 1.1; the expression digest and Boolean evaluate method retain their existing behavior.

from rigor_foundry.condition_evaluation import evaluate_condition_state
from rigor_foundry.condition_facts import ConditionFact, ConditionTruth
from rigor_foundry.condition_language import ConditionExpression

expression = ConditionExpression.build("exists", reference="project.enabled")

assert evaluate_condition_state(expression, {}) is ConditionTruth.UNKNOWN
assert evaluate_condition_state(
    expression, {"project.enabled": ConditionFact.known(None)}
) is ConditionTruth.TRUE
assert evaluate_condition_state(
    expression, {"project.enabled": ConditionFact.absent()}
) is ConditionTruth.FALSE

A known None is an observed JSON null, so exists is true. Declared absence makes a leaf false. An omitted reference or ConditionFact.unknown() stays unknown, including under negation. A parent observation never manufactures observations for its missing descendants. A known descendant conflicting with an observed scalar or absent parent refuses. An unobserved parent permits a separately observed descendant; unknown is not evidence of a contradiction.

Facts contain finite JSON scalars or immutable flat scalar tuples. Parsing an array copies its elements into a tuple. Nested objects, non-finite numbers, malformed references and a value attached to absent/unknown refuse. Observation equality and hashing preserve exact serialized data, including the difference between Boolean true and numeric1.

Inputs are supplied operands. Authenticating their producer, snapshot and maintained source/language scope belongs to the selected policy consumer. The calculation supplies no permission or gate acceptance.

docs.title: Three-valued groups
docs.text:
Left Right all any true true true true true false false true true unknown unknown true false true false true false false false false false unknown false unknown unknown true unknown true unknown false false unknown unknown unknown unknown unknown

Negation maps true to false, false to true, and unknown to unknown. Every known operand is checked even after a decisive sibling: a bad numeric comparison cannot disappear behind a true any or false all.

Known leaves use the original operator implementation, including numeric versus Boolean identity and string/array containment. Explicit absence is false for every leaf; unknown is never passed to the old evaluator as an empty mapping.

Compare results explicitly. bool(ConditionTruth.FALSE) and bool(ConditionTruth.UNKNOWN) raise TypeError; the strings must not become truthy guards. Trees retain the existing depth8/node64 limits. The evaluator accepts at most65,536 observations.

docs.title: Module command
docs.text:
Run the separately versioned provisional command:

python -m rigor_foundry.condition_evaluation_cli --expression expression.json --observations observations.json

expression.json is the complete digest-bound output of ConditionExpression.to_dict(). Create one through the existing builder:

import json
from pathlib import Path
from rigor_foundry.condition_language import ConditionExpression

expression = ConditionExpression.build("eq", reference="project.enabled", value=True)
Path("expression.json").write_text(json.dumps(expression.to_dict()), encoding="utf-8")

observations.json has exactly these fields:

{
  "schema_version": "rigor.condition-observations.v1",
  "facts": {
    "project.enabled": {"state": "known", "value": true}
  }
}

Each fact has exactly state and value. States are known, absent and unknown. The latter two require null. An empty facts object means missing knowledge. This operand format is not an authenticated task or fact context; extra provenance fields are rejected rather than trusted.

The JSON result uses rigor.condition-evaluation.v1 and has exactly schema_version, evaluation_kind, expression_digest, observations_digest, result and guard_admissible. evaluation_kind is supplied-observations; guard_admissible is always false. The two digests identify the parsed expression and canonical operand data, not trusted source custody. No raw observation values appear in output.

Exit Meaning 0 Supplied condition evaluates true 1 Supplied condition evaluates false 2 Invalid arguments, file, JSON, expression or operand 3 Supplied condition remains unknown

Each explicit input is limited to64KiB and read through single-link regular-file, no-follow descriptors. Duplicate keys, non-finite numbers, symlinks, hardlinks, directories, stale expression digests and oversized files refuse. Diagnostic CE001 does not echo paths, values or raw exceptions. The command writes only its result to stdout. It performs no audit, process dispatch, signing or source discovery.

The frozen rigor1.0 command inventory remains unchanged. This module command and the module-level Python APIs are provisional; their explicit record versions remain independent of that older CLI inventory.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Without an adopter policy, RigorFoundry uses portable defaults and emits a governance candidate explaining that the repository-specific contract is missing.

Policy discovery is deterministic:

  1. an explicit repository-relative CLI path;
  2. rigor-foundry-policy.json;
  3. config/rigor-foundry/policy.json.

The selected policy must be a tracked, non-symlink UTF-8 file inside the audited repository. External, parent-relative, ignored, and symlinked policy inputs fail closed rather than silently controlling the audit.

rigor bootstrap creates a starting policy only when the adopter explicitly names the policy, canonical TODO, review ledger, and every source/test root. The policy path must be trackable; internal paths must already be Git-ignored. Parents and code roots must already exist. The generated policy uses observe mode, production/test line thresholds of 700/1000, and marks all audit domains required. It does not infer applicability, production packages, size registries, native commands, or internal paths. Review those fields before the first baseline; see First repository.

docs.title: Candidate anchor schemas
docs.text:
Candidate-anchor schema 1.0 is a strict discriminated union:

  • tracked-blob binds a canonical path, inclusive line span, scanned Git blob identity, and content SHA-256;
  • repository-tree binds a path locus, fixed state span 1:1, HEAD tree identity, and complete tracked-content SHA-256.

Report schema 1.3 requires one anchor on every candidate and records git_object_format. Scanner version 0.3.0 verifies all anchors against the inventory that produced the report. Campaign schema 1.5 carries the object format into independent-run input comparison. Campaign schema 1.9 additionally binds ignored inventory, campaign purpose, witness requirements, explicit inference identity, and structured built-in adapter evidence. Earlier report or campaign records must be regenerated; unknown or mixed anchor fields have no compatibility fallback.

Repository policy controls source and test roots, production packages, mandatory audit domains, size registries, enforcement mode, the expected rule-maturity policy digest, and declared native adapters. The desired-state API adds typed adopter variables, namespaced custom controls, applicability decisions, exact standard-pack selections, and secret-provider references.

Source and test roots are interpreted as repository-relative component sequences; absolute and parent-traversing values never match. A source root must prefix a path by whole components; when roots overlap, the longest component sequence owns the module. A test root may occur below a workspace prefix, but it must match complete contiguous components, so tests does not match contest or tests-old. Common test_, _test.py, .test., and .spec. conventions apply to the generic scanners. Polyglot ownership additionally recognises native _test.<suffix> and _tests.<suffix> names. These naming profiles are fixed scanner capabilities, not policy-controlled aliases. Python module ownership deliberately preserves the narrower historical contract: configured test roots are repository prefixes, and only test_/_test.py names apply outside them.

docs.title: Declared ignored inventory
docs.text:
Policy schema 1.3 and later accept an ignored_inventory array sorted by evidence_id, path, and capture. Every declaration contains a unique portable evidence_id, a unique exact normalised repository-relative path, and presence, file-sha256, or directory-sha256. Globs, absolute paths, parent traversal, tracked paths, and paths outside Git ignore rules are rejected.

Collection never records file content, symlink targets, environment values, or undeclared roots. directory-sha256 recursively hashes only the declared tree through descriptor-relative no-follow reads, stores byte paths as hexadecimal inside a versioned canonical manifest, and caps depth, entry count, and total regular-file bytes. Evidence is limited to observed, missing, or unavailable, the observed entry kind, bounded byte size, an optional SHA-256, and a finite reason. Symlinks, special files, hard links, resource-limit breaches, and concurrent mutation fail closed. Missing and unavailable observations are evidence gaps, not automatic control failures.

docs.title: Rule-maturity policy and cases
docs.text:
Rule-maturity policy is deliberately separate from repository scan policy. It controls whether a rule may influence ratchet or zero enforcement, not whether the scanner may emit a candidate. The schema-1.0 policy requires these exact integer fields and its canonical policy_digest:

  • minimum_adjudicated_reviews;
  • minimum_distinct_repositories;
  • minimum_distinct_reviewers;
  • minimum_positive_reviews;
  • maximum_false_positive_basis_points, from 0 through 10,000;
  • maximum_median_effort_seconds; and
  • maximum_p90_effort_seconds.

All minima are at least one, positive reviews cannot exceed the total review minimum, and the median limit cannot exceed the p90 limit. RigorFoundry supplies no universal threshold values; adopters must justify them against their corpus and operating costs.

Repository policy schema 1.3 binds that separate calibration through maturity_policy_digest. Observe mode may leave it null, but a repository whose enforcement_mode is ratchet or zero must name the exact 64-character lowercase policy digest. A CLI request may strengthen observe mode only when the repository already binds the supplied maturity report's policy digest. Consequently an operator cannot select an empty or weaker calibration report at gate time and silently turn repository candidates into probation.

The case manifest has exact top-level fields schema_version, policy, and cases. Every case has repository_id, report, review, candidate_id, reviewer_effort_seconds, and non-empty effort_evidence. A source-validated case projects the exact tree, tracked-content, scan-policy, report, candidate, rule, review, reviewer, decision, timestamp, duration, and effort references into one evidence digest. Reusing the same report/candidate pair twice is rejected. The resulting maturity report binds the current rule-pack version and digest, complete threshold policy, sorted evidence, all rule assessments, and one maturity_digest.

docs.title: External source retrieval policy
docs.text: External source provenance uses a standalone schema 1.0 retrieval policy; it is not silently inherited from repository scan policy. The policy requires a sorted unique host allowlist, explicit cross-origin redirect decision, at most ten redirects, positive timeout and freshness bounds, a byte limit no greater than 32 MiB, and sorted lowercase media types without parameters. Capture metadata must reproduce the complete policy and its digest. See Verified external source provenance.

docs.title: Git executable trust
docs.text:
Git bootstrap trust is runtime configuration, not repository-controlled policy: the audited repository cannot choose which executable reads its own index. By default, RigorFoundry searches the basename git only in fixed platform roots, never in ambient PATH. The default supported interval is Git 2.35.2 or newer and lower than 3.0.0.

Every Git-using CLI command accepts the same controls:

rigor scan --root /workspace \
  --git-executable /opt/toolchain/bin/git \
  --git-trust-root /opt/toolchain/bin \
  --git-min-version 2.43.0 \
  --git-max-version-exclusive 3.0.0

--git-trust-root is repeatable and ordered. Roots must be normalised absolute directories. An absolute executable requires at least one explicit root; a relative executable must be one basename and is searched only below the roots. The root, intervening components, and executable must not be symlinks. The executable must be a single-link regular file; POSIX mode checks also reject group/world-write, set-user-ID, and set-group-ID bits. Each Git invocation overrides repository-local core.fsmonitor and core.hooksPath. Hooks are redirected to a reserved absent directory below the selected trust root; if that reserved path exists, execution fails closed. Execution also fails closed on platforms that cannot execute the already validated open descriptor. campaign-run must receive the same explicit options used by campaign-create; otherwise frozen Git provenance diverges and the run is rejected. It must also receive explicit provider, exact-model, model-correlation-family, and operator identities. These values are evidence, not labels inferred from a session or agent name. Operator declarations must be authenticated by the surrounding deployment; the campaign record does not claim a cryptographic operator signature.

Python callers pass GitTrustPolicy through the keyword-only git_trust_policy argument of scan_repository, load_git_inventory, campaign workflow functions, ignored-path storage, or TODO promotion. The durable report records GitExecutableProvenance: resolved path, selected root, parsed version, executable SHA-256, complete versioned trust policy, derived policy SHA-256, and its own identity digest. Portable policy JSON uses canonical forward-slash POSIX or Windows absolute paths and can be verified on another host. The trust root is an operator assertion and must be protected from untrusted writers. Campaign storage and TODO promotion reproduce the report or campaign identity before using Git ignore rules; a different policy-compliant binary is still treated as input divergence.

docs.title: Classified coverage residuals
docs.text:
Repository self-governance uses the tracked coverage-residuals.json manifest. It is separate from adopter audit policy because it describes this tool's own test-evidence boundary, not a finding in the repository being audited.

Each residual must identify one exact source symbol and guard, bind the symbol's SHA-256, use one of platform-primitive, runtime-invariant, or race-window, name an accountable owner, cite public regression tests, list specific revisit triggers, and expire no later than 90 days after review. A source edit, removed guard, missing test, expired review, unknown field, or duplicate identifier fails validation.

The manifest also contains preregistered regular-expression searches over explicit test owners. Their expected result is empty. They currently reject private production-helper calls, object.__new__ construction, monkeypatched production internals, and direct use of the private preflight runner.

Validate the contract directly with:

rigor residuals-check --root .

python -m tools.audit, make audit, local preflight, and the CI quality job run the same validator. Residuals never count as covered lines and do not lower the aggregate branch-coverage threshold.

Repository guard CLIs print only fixed pass/fail status. Precise diagnostic strings remain available to trusted in-process callers, while validation exceptions also fail closed without a traceback. Neither enters shared logs, because repository paths and metadata can be attacker-controlled. The secret guard additionally replaces every programmatic path with its full SHA-256 identifier.

docs.title: Desired-state inputs
docs.text:
A StandardPack defines versioned controls, evidence contracts, remediation contracts, licence and source metadata, a detached signature envelope, and a content digest. A ProjectProfile selects exact pack versions and digests and records project intent without copying or weakening the pack silently.

Standard-pack schema 1.1, signature-envelope schema 1.0, and pack-verification schema 1.0 require and bind the rigor-foundry.standard-pack.v1 signature domain. Reviewer-attestation schema 2.0 requires rigor-foundry.reviewer-attestation.v1. Both sign the public ed25519_signature_message() encoding: the fixed RIGOR-FOUNDRY-ED25519\0v1\0 prefix, a two-byte big-endian domain length, the ASCII domain, and the 32 payload-digest bytes. Earlier pack schema 1.0, unversioned reviewer records, missing domains, and raw-digest signatures must be regenerated and re-signed; the parser and verifier provide no legacy fallback.

Project variables support string, integer, number, boolean, and string-list values. Every variable declares project, environment, or control scope and public, internal, or secret sensitivity.
