docs.title: Deliberate stable non-edges
docs.text:
• A candidate-only report change does not change the campaign contract. A campaign freezes scanner inputs, not one scanner output. It does change the report, report diff, rebound review, task, and closure identities.
  • Standard packs, adapter locks, and effective-profile locks form a separate desired-state subgraph. Current repository reports and campaigns do not bind that lock, although the same toolchain identity can independently affect a campaign contract and an effective-profile lock.
  • A standard-pack mutation does not change an adapter lock, and an adapter-lock mutation does not change a standard pack. Both change an effective-profile lock that contains them.
  • Review rationale, evidence, reviewer, and time can change a review and any resulting task without changing the source report or campaign.
  • A maturity report may contain no adjudications, so report and review are not unconditional graph parents. Each populated maturity evidence row does bind its exact report_digest, candidate identifier, and review_digest; the report recomputes those conditional member identities. Likewise, observe-mode enforcement may omit maturity, while ratchet and zero require and bind it.
  • External source provenance is a separate evidence subgraph. Current reports, profiles, waivers, and standard packs do not unconditionally consume it. Consumers must reference a specific verification digest in a separately versioned schema migration rather than infer authority from source presence.
  • Offline verification is an evidence-consumer subgraph. It binds exact reports, packs, review evidence, model-alias collapse, detached signatures, the selected lifecycle trust policy, bundle, and per-entry results. It does not feed authority back into source reports, assurance campaigns, profiles, enforcement, fleet state, or remediation plans.
  • Comparison logic embeds the exact participating attestation, report, and review digests, plus the collapsed model-witness identities. The set of participating records is campaign-instance data rather than a fixed schema dependency, so only the campaign contract remains an unconditional normative comparison edge. A run attestation separately binds its campaign contract, report, toolchain, and any adapter-profile evidence; it is not part of the earlier campaign identity. Promotion reconstructs the conditional comparison bindings from durable records before accepting a selected report and review.

These non-edges are compatibility contracts, not omissions hidden by the diagram. Adding a new binding requires a schema/version migration and updated mutation and non-interference vectors.

docs.title: Proof requirements
docs.text:
The owning schema tests rebuild production records through public constructors. For each declared upstream class they assert both sides of the contract:

  1. the upstream identity and every reachable dependent identity change; and
  2. every unrelated identity in the exercised graph remains byte-for-byte stable.

The tests compare all 32 identities and cover inventory, ignored inventory, Git provenance, policy, rule-pack, maturity policy, rule maturity, toolchain, adapter-profile, report, report diff, review, campaign, run attestation, task, adapter-lock, standard-pack, effective-profile, closure, source claim, retrieval policy, capture, source verification, verification-key policy, offline trust policy, model aliases, evidence signatures, review evidence, verification bundles, verification results, and offline verification reports. Strict parsing vectors reject altered closure schemas, fields, references, counts, and digests. An archived work record and its original closed record reproduce the same closure identity.

docs.title: Dispatch permit candidates
docs.text: The provisional module-level Python API rigor_foundry.instruction_dispatch_permit_v2 parses and verifies one signed candidate decision. Its wire schema is instruction-dispatch-permit.v2.1 and its signature domain is rigor-foundry.instruction-dispatch-permit.v2.1. Legacy v1 and earlier v2 domains are refused. The named schema declaration is version-pinned in the provisional schema inventory; the frozen 1.0 contract, package-level exports and CLI remain unchanged.

docs.title: Public API
docs.text:
Surface Responsibility RuleChainV2PermitTrustRoles.build(chain=..., permit_issuers=...) Rebuild caller-selected policies and require six distinct signing roles. DispatchPermitBodyV2.from_dict(value) / to_dict() Validate the exact body and canonical payload digest. SignedDispatchPermitV2.build(body=..., signature_hex=...) Bind external signature bytes to a rebuilt body and envelope digests. SignedDispatchPermitV2.from_dict(value) / to_dict() Parse exact wire fields or export retained fields. verify_signature(roles=..., now=...) Rebuild the envelope and policies, then check the actual Ed25519 signature and key lifecycle with caller-supplied UTC time.

build and from_dict reject invalid structure with ValueError. Signature verification returns False for invalid candidate values, reused roles, wrong signature domain, inactive issuer or an invalid time window. Envelope export rechecks the body; complete envelope validation occurs in from_dict and verify_signature, including directly constructed instances.

docs.title: Exact signed decision
docs.text:
The body contains exactly these fields:

  • schema_version, object_kind, signature_domain, algorithm, signer_role;
  • permit_id, key_id, issued_at, not_before, expires_at;
  • lock_digest, rule_projection_digest, request_digest, grant_snapshot_digest, current_state_proof_digest, adapter_custody_digest, route_digest, effect_target_digest, effect_operations_digest, operations_digest.

The constants are respectively instruction-dispatch-permit.v2.1, instruction-dispatch-permit, the domain above, ed25519 and permit-issuer. The permit ID must be canonical UUID text, excluding all-zero and all-one IDs. Every decision digest is a lowercase 64-character SHA-256 representation. No unknown or missing fields receive defaults.

The signed envelope adds payload_digest, signature_hex, signature_digest and permit_digest. The signature is 64 bytes represented by 128 lowercase hex characters. Digests bind canonical body and envelope bytes; parsing their consistency does not establish signature validity.

docs.title: Six separate policies and bounded time
docs.text:
The permit issuer must be distinct from pack issuer, project selector, lock resolver, semantic author and semantic reviewer. Reuse is refused by both key ID and public key bytes, including a semantic-author key enrolled under a new permit ID. Verification repeats role composition, so directly constructing a role dataclass cannot bypass separation. The underlying chain also retains its semantic author/reviewer identity checks.

All body timestamps use canonical UTC representations. Issuance cannot follow the start; the start must be within five seconds of issuance. The positive validity window is at most 300 seconds. Verification requires issued_at <= not_before <= now < expires_at and an active issuer at issuance, start and the supplied current time. The expiry endpoint is excluded.

A consumer with an externally signed wire candidate and explicitly selected policies can use:

from rigor_foundry.instruction_dispatch_permit_v2 import (
    RuleChainV2PermitTrustRoles,
    SignedDispatchPermitV2,
)

roles = RuleChainV2PermitTrustRoles.build(
    chain=selected_chain_policies,
    permit_issuers=selected_permit_issuer_policy,
)
candidate = SignedDispatchPermitV2.from_dict(signed_wire_mapping)
valid_signature = candidate.verify_signature(roles=roles, now=selected_utc_time)

The names supplied to this example are consumer inputs. The library does not select policies, enroll keys, produce signatures or authenticate the clock.

docs.title: Host admission remains separate
docs.text: A valid signature binds the supplied decision digests without proving that they describe the current host. A qualified host must select protected trust and current state, authenticate its own clock, verify applicability and atomically consume the permit ID before any registered effect. This candidate API performs no handler execution and supplies no admission or consumption method. The selected dispatch applicability API and permit consumption ledger are separate components; this module does not compose an executable dispatch path.

docs.title: Documentation, claims, and IP rules
docs.text: Rule-pack rigor-foundry/1.12.0 adds a bounded documentation category (prefix DC). Each finding is an anchored needs-evidence candidate, not a licence verdict, infringement claim, compatibility verdict, or proof that published documentation is otherwise complete.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rule Signal Confidence DC001-missing-license-header a tracked UTF-8 source owner under a policy-declared source root has no SPDX-License-Identifier declaration in its first five lines high DC002-doc-version-drift an explicit distribution-version statement in a public README or documentation page differs from static PEP 621 project metadata high

DC001 applies to the source suffixes already owned by the responsibility scanner: Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, Rust, C/C++, Julia, Shell, Lean, Mojo, Verilog, and SystemVerilog. The source must be under an exact source_roots prefix from the repository policy. Binary, non-UTF-8, out-of-root, test-only, prose, and configuration files are not classified by this rule. The five-line window admits an interpreter shebang and encoding declaration while retaining the meaning of a leading header. The rule checks only that an SPDX licence declaration exists; it does not decide whether the expression is legally correct or whether separate copyright text is required.

DC002 requires one tracked root pyproject.toml with static string [project].name and [project].version fields. It recognises explicit current guidance such as distribution==1.2.3, distribution v1.2.3, and distribution version 1.2.3, including normalised -, _, and . name separators and optional extras. Root README files and Markdown or reStructuredText pages under docs/ are in scope. Changelogs, histories, release notes, docs/internal/, unrelated root prose, and other suffixes are excluded so historical version records are not misclassified as current guidance. Missing, dynamic, malformed, or non-static project metadata produces no DC002 candidate and must not be interpreted as evidence that documentation versions agree.

docs.title: Evidence and verification
docs.text:
Candidates contain exact tracked-blob anchors and content digests without copying source or documentation text into the report. DC002 additionally binds SHA-256 identities of the expected version and distribution name. Review DC001 against the repository's actual licence ownership before adding the correct SPDX expression. Review DC002 against [project].version, then update current installation or compatibility guidance or move genuinely historical statements to an excluded historical surface.

The family contributes a portable control to the documentation-claims-ip audit domain. Both rules enter maturity probation; safe and vulnerable fixtures establish scanner behaviour, while adjudicated false-positive and reviewer-effort evidence across adopter repositories is a separate activation gate.

docs.title: Fuzzing
docs.text: RigorFoundry parses untrusted, content-addressed audit records — reports, candidates, review ledgers, and policies — that may arrive from other tools or adopters. Every parser is contractually fail-closed: hostile or malformed input must raise ValueError, never crash with an unexpected exception or hang. Coverage-guided fuzzing verifies that contract continuously.

docs.title: Harness
docs.text:
The fuzz/ directory holds Atheris coverage-guided fuzz targets, one per untrusted-input parser:

Target Parser under test fuzz/fuzz_audit_report.py AuditReport.from_dict fuzz/fuzz_candidate.py Candidate.from_dict fuzz/fuzz_audit_policy.py AuditPolicy.from_json fuzz/fuzz_review_record.py ReviewRecord.from_dict

Each target feeds fuzzer-derived bytes across the JSON boundary through the shared helpers in fuzz/_record_fuzz.py. The helpers tolerate only the contractual failure modes — ValueError (its fail-closed contract, of which UnicodeDecodeError and json.JSONDecodeError are subclasses) and RecursionError (CPython's bounded response to deeply nested input). Any other exception propagates so the fuzzer records it as a genuine robustness finding.

docs.title: Running locally
docs.text:
Install the hash-locked fuzzing environment (Atheris ships wheels for CPython 3.12 and newer) and run a target for a bounded time:

python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements/fuzz.txt
python -m pip install --no-build-isolation --no-deps .
python fuzz/fuzz_audit_report.py -max_total_time=60

A crash writes a reproducer file to the working directory; replay it by passing the file as an argument.

docs.title: Continuous integration
docs.text: The Fuzz workflow (.github/workflows/fuzz.yml) runs every target for a bounded interval on each pull request, on main, and on a weekly schedule, failing the job on any crash. The targets are not pytest tests and are not collected by the suite; they exercise the parsers as adversarial input handlers rather than as behavioural unit tests.

docs.title: First repository
docs.text: This tutorial creates an adopter-owned policy and private work ledger without letting RigorFoundry guess their locations or overwrite existing project data.

docs.title: Install and identify the tool
docs.text:
Use an exact published version or a reviewed source checkout, then record the version that will create the policy:

python -m pip install "rigor-foundry==0.1.1"
rigor --version

The expected output is rigor 0.1.1. A policy, report, or campaign remains bound to its own schema and scanner identities; the package version is not a substitute for those content identities.

docs.title: Declare private paths first
docs.text:
From the root of the Git worktree, create the parent of the internal ledger and make Git ignore the exact internal namespace. The policy itself must remain trackable:

mkdir -p docs/internal
printf '%s\n' 'docs/internal/' >> .gitignore
git check-ignore --quiet --no-index docs/internal/TODO.md
git check-ignore --quiet --no-index docs/internal/reviews.json

Review .gitignore before committing it. Do not use a broad rule that hides the policy or production source.

docs.title: Bootstrap explicit paths
docs.text:
Pass every adopter-owned path and every current source/test root. Repeat --source-root or --test-root for additional roots:

rigor bootstrap \
  --root . \
  --policy rigor-foundry-policy.json \
  --todo docs/internal/TODO.md \
  --review-ledger docs/internal/reviews.json \
  --source-root src \
  --test-root tests

Bootstrap succeeds only when:

  • --root is the exact real Git worktree root, not a symlink or subdirectory;
  • source/test roots and the parents of new files already exist without symlink components;
  • the policy path is untracked, absent, and not ignored;
  • TODO and review-ledger paths are untracked and already ignored; and
  • policy, TODO, and review-ledger paths are distinct and repository relative.

The command creates the policy as a regular 0644 file and the canonical TODO as a private 0600 file. It never creates the review ledger and rejects one present at either validation sample. Ledger absence is not reserved atomically: a concurrent owner can populate the declared path after the final sample. The command does not guess a TODO, create parents, follow symlinks, or overwrite an existing path. If a concurrent mutation or second-file failure occurs after one file is created, bootstrap fails and preserves the created evidence. Inspect it before retrying; the tool never performs a pathname-based rollback that could delete a concurrent writer's replacement.

docs.title: Review the fail-closed policy
docs.text:
The generated policy starts in observe mode with a 700-line production threshold, a 1000-line test threshold, and every audit domain marked required. This is deliberate: RigorFoundry cannot infer which security, architecture, compliance, performance, or operational domains apply to a new repository.

Before treating scan output as a project gate:

  1. Review every audit_domains entry and record repository-specific evidence for any not-applicable decision.
  2. Add production-package roots, module-size registries, and native adapters that are actually owned and executable in the adopter environment.
  3. Review thresholds and keep enforcement in observe until the baseline and review ledger are evidence-bound.
  4. Commit the policy and .gitignore; keep the canonical TODO and review ledger ignored.

docs.title: Run the first read-only scan
docs.text:
rigor scan \
  --root . \
  --policy rigor-foundry-policy.json \
  --json-out docs/internal/first-report.json

The report contains candidates, not verdicts. Undeclared controls, missing native evidence, and unresolved domain decisions must remain visible rather than being converted into a clean result. Use review-template, validate-review, and an independent campaign before promoting a verified finding into the canonical TODO.

docs.title: Add a repository gate
docs.text: After committing the reviewed policy, adopt the pinned GitHub Action or pre-commit hook from Consumer integrations. Create and ignore the exact report parent first. Begin in observe mode; ratchet and zero require an explicit maturity report already bound by policy. Neither integration can apply remediation or promote findings.

docs.title: Git command provenance and resource bounds
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.git_provenance.GitRunner runs Git through an inspected, descriptor-pinned executable. Its trust policy selects executable roots and a supported version interval. Each command checks executable content and filesystem identity before and after execution. Ambient PATH, global and system Git configuration, replacement objects, optional locks and interactive credentials do not select the command. Reserved command configuration disables repository hooks and filesystem monitors.

Executable inspection opens the leaf with nonblocking I/O before checking its actual descriptor type. A FIFO cannot block that regular-file check.

The public run(cwd, *arguments, check=True, timeout_seconds=30, output_limit=8388608) method uses the shared streaming process runner. Its output ceiling counts standard output and standard error together. It is checked during reading; an over-limit result raises rather than returning a truncated inventory. Exactly the permitted number of bytes succeeds. Version discovery has a separate 4096-byte ceiling. Timeout and output limits must be positive integers; boolean values are refused.

The command deadline covers output collection and waiting for the leader after its pipes close. On timeout or output exhaustion the runner terminates the process group and reaps its leader. No shell interprets the arguments. Standard output and standard error remain bytes, including binary Git objects and NUL separators. check=False returns a bounded nonzero result; check=True raises on a nonzero exit without including the command's output in the exception message.

from pathlib import Path

from rigor_foundry.git_provenance import GitRunner

runner = GitRunner()
result = runner.run(
    Path.cwd(), "ls-files", "--stage", "-z", output_limit=1024 * 1024
)
index_bytes = result.stdout

Callers supply an output budget appropriate to their admitted inventory and parse the complete result. These limits do not establish inventory completeness, source-access permission, snapshot atomicity, policy admission or native-effect authority. Descriptor execution requires an available /proc/self/fd or /dev/fd; the process-group implementation requires POSIX process facilities.

RigorFoundry — portable GitHub Actions candidate rules
GitHub Actions security candidates
docs.text:
The read-only repository scanner inspects tracked YAML directly inside .github/workflows and tracked action.yml/action.yaml metadata. It never runs a workflow, resolves an action over the network, evaluates an expression, or constructs Python objects from YAML. All four new rules enter the 1.19.0 rule pack in probation. Passing author tests supplies no adjudicated calibration evidence and does not activate enforcement.

Rule Source signal Verification GA001-unpinned-action-reference Actual step action or job reusable-workflow reference lacks an immutable pin. Review upstream ownership and the exact revision before choosing a full 40-digit commit SHA or Docker SHA-256 digest. GA002-run-context-interpolation A run value directly interpolates event data, a branch name or an input. Trace the trigger and script language; prefer an intermediate environment variable with appropriate quoting. GA003-pull-request-target-checkout A target-event checkout selects PR head/merge/fork code or an unresolved dynamic source. Review permissions, secrets, downstream execution and checkout protections. GV006-unscanned-github-actions A relevant tracked owner is unreadable, malformed, ambiguous, unsupported or over budget. Resolve the exact incomplete owner before making a clean claim.

docs.title: Structural and source boundaries
docs.text:
GA001 reads executable uses positions rather than every matching YAML key. It includes composite action steps, local actions and reusable workflows. Local relative references need no external revision pin; parent traversal and expression-bearing local references are not accepted as immutable local pins. External actions require a full commit SHA; Docker references require a full SHA-256 digest. A pin establishes source identity, not upstream trust.

GA002 examines actual run values. Expressions in env, with, if and concurrency are not inline scripts. Shell comments and quotes do not prevent GitHub's earlier expression substitution. Constant expression strings and the known commit SHA/PR-number/issue-number paths have distinct safe controls. Other github.event paths, github.head_ref, github.ref_name, the whole github context and inputs require review. Dot and constant bracket access are equivalent; dynamic event access preserves its untrusted prefix.

GA003 distinguishes pull_request_target from pull_request and supports scalar, sequence and mapping event declarations. Default checkout and known target base identities are controls. PR head/fork selection, refs/pull selectors and unresolved dynamic checkout contexts require review. A hardcoded revision's origin cannot be inferred from its spelling. A candidate does not prove that untrusted code ran: modern checkout versions have fork checkout protections, including an explicit allow-unsafe-pr-checkout input.

An expression is a trusted base control only when the complete input is one exact trusted context property or one literal string outside refs/pull/ after input padding is removed. Functions, operators, multiple substitutions and mixtures of literal text and substitutions remain unresolved and require review. A trusted property inside a larger expression does not establish the resulting checkout identity. For example, ${{ format('refs/{0}/42/merge', 'pull') }} and refs/${{ 'pull' }}/42/head both require review. The scanner does not evaluate these expressions; see GitHub's expression reference.

Literal controls follow the checkout input reader's surrounding-whitespace normalisation, including no-break spaces and the byte-order mark. Padding a PR ref must not turn it into a benign literal. This follows the default getInput contract and ECMAScript's trim semantics. The source spelling and tracked-blob anchor remain unchanged by this analysis.

YAML parsing retains literal on keys and physical inclusive line spans. No YAML 1.1 boolean conversion can erase the event declaration. Backward, acyclic aliases use immutable values anchored at their original definitions. Duplicate keys/anchors, cycles/forward aliases, merge keys, custom tags, tag-shape mismatches and multiple documents refuse explicitly. Parsing is limited to 1 MiB UTF-8, 8192 events, 32 nested value levels and 128 aliases. These limits apply before building a larger representation. The underlying Git inventory's separate text/binary/symlink limits still apply. Analysis also permits at most 4096 job/step occurrences per owner, counting alias-expanded executable positions before inspection. This prevents a small aliased YAML graph from multiplying scanner work or candidate allocations.

Candidates retain exact tracked blob identities and source spans. Their evidence contains file/span digests and fixed diagnostic reasons, rather than scripts or attacker-controlled values. Symbols use structural positions, not user-supplied job names. JSON report and SARIF exports preserve candidate state; confidence is not severity or an accepted finding.

docs.title: Verification and limitations
docs.text:
Dedicated public tests exercise real YAML, Git repositories, repository scan, CLI failure status, report round trips, SARIF, source anchors, non-mutation, probation and positive/negative controls for all three security rules. The scanner does not implement the entire GitHub workflow schema, evaluate expressions, resolve remote reusable workflows, propagate caller events into local/composite actions, or perform shell/data-flow analysis. JavaScript and Docker action execution bodies remain separate analysis surfaces. The expression check is lexical and does not certify general expression validity. An unexplained GV006 prevents claiming that its owner was completely scanned.

The lexer retains an unterminated-string guard behind quote-balanced expression extraction. The YAML reader also retains a guard against unexpected native event kinds at value positions. Their source-bound, expiring entries in coverage-residuals.json name the surrounding public regressions and conditions for revisiting the classification. The same manifest rejects specified private parser access and simulated internals in the workflow tests. These records supply no coverage credit and do not waive a coverage threshold or establish that every possible public input has been examined.

Rule-pack identity changes to 1.19.0. Existing rule introduction versions and serialized record field layouts remain unchanged. Version-bound report and maturity readers continue to require their exact scanner rule pack; retain the matching reader with historical evidence. The published 1.0 calibration corpus is historical and supplies no evidence for these new rules.

The implementation follows GitHub's script injection guidance, immutable action reference guidance and current target-event checkout guidance. PyYAML's parser documentation distinguishes event parsing from application object construction.

docs.title: Instruction-scoped dispatch
docs.text:
instruction_dispatch.dispatch_instruction_action resolves host-authenticated instructions before invoking a registered operation. It is a cooperative Python integration API, not a deployed policy service, sandbox or signed grant parser.

ActionScope binds actor, runtime, project, task, effect, exact target and the provider/account/cost/privacy route. InstructionScope selects exact values; None explicitly leaves a dimension unrestricted. Targets are opaque identifiers: the owning adapter must canonicalise paths and retain filesystem custody. There is no prefix matching, path expansion or inferred provider fallback.

Supply InstructionPolicy from trusted host composition. Its issuer order is highest-first, and its explicit grantors may issue permission. Documents, roles and request fields cannot create that authority. Instructions sharing a subject are resolved by applicable scope, explicit same-subject supersession and issuer precedence. Equal-authority contradictions and override cycles refuse the affected action. Independent subjects remain constraints. A surviving permission allow from an authorised grantor is mandatory; absence of a prohibition is not a grant. Existing audit-profile deny/waiver rules and independent remediation approval are unchanged. Different action scopes can resolve independently.

Construct an immutable DispatchRequest with exact actions, existing AdapterLock, route and payload bytes. A trusted state factory acquires a DispatchLease for that exact request. It must authenticate policy, verify the registered adapter's effects from the payload, observe current availability and retain resource/target custody. Matching advertisement is necessary but is not effect verification. The lease binds the actual handler, not an arbitrary callback supplied by a caller.

Dispatch requires matching advertised and verified adapter locks, identical verified effects, identical route, and available OS capability. After resolution, the host's revalidate checks current expiry, revocation, resource allowances and executable/target identity immediately before invocation. The handler receives the same immutable payload used in preparation. The host holds its lease until the handler returns or fails. Suppressed errors become an explicit failure, not a successful empty result. No automatic account or billing fallback is attempted.

docs.title: Evidence and limits
docs.text:
Never expose the state factory, policy ordering, grantor set, verified effects or handler registration as unauthenticated request inputs. This API cannot certify truthfulness of host assertions, contain hostile same-process code, authenticate a general signed dispatch grant, enforce arbitrary resource budgets itself or cancel an already admitted operation. Use the existing native sandbox and trusted executable custody where applicable. The signed campaign permit remains specific to campaign creation and cannot authorise these general operations.

Tests exercise actual local file writes and reads, including forbidden writes leaving bytes unchanged. They verify the in-process composition contract, not a hosted provider, remote publication or cross-process enforcement deployment. The documentation gate checks every declaration in this maintained cohort, including private/nested/test definitions. Presence checks do not prove meaningful documentation; review still owns that judgement.

The maintained acceptance cohort names all fourteen ratified boundary cases. It uses real local file bytes and a loopback HTTP service to observe forbidden transport independently of decision text. These tests establish the cooperative dispatch contract only; they do not certify a hosted Git provider, production consumer registration, deployment or rollout.

docs.title: Signed operation and policy binding
docs.text:
signed_instruction_dispatch.dispatch_signed_instruction_action composes the same dispatcher with a dedicated SignedDispatchPermit. The permit binds dispatch_request_digest(request) and instruction_policy_digest(policy), issuer and explicit issuance/expiry times. Sign its payload_digest using the existing Ed25519 encoder and DISPATCH_SIGNATURE_DOMAIN. Campaign or report signatures cannot substitute. Request identity includes actual payload bytes by digest and all effect, adapter and route fields. Policy identity includes every source, selector, override edge, grantor and the semantically ordered issuer list.

The host supplies a fresh context containing SignedDispatchState: its registered lease, the permit, dedicated OfflineTrustPolicy and current revoked permit payloads. The wrapper first performs existing dispatch checks, then calls the host's custody revalidation. Immediately afterwards it checks exact bindings, the real signature and current issuer/permit validity, before invoking the handler. Its clock and state/trust configuration must not come from untrusted request data. No default validity interval, cached permission or silent trust fallback exists.

This proves the dedicated issuer approved these exact request and policy bytes. It does not independently authenticate every referenced policy document or verify the adapter's effect claims. Registered production providers still own truthful effects, current resource availability, executable/target custody and isolation. The signed API adds no wire parser or automatic production consumer cutover.

docs.title: Opt-in native audit consumer
docs.text:
native_dispatch.dispatch_native_audit is the first concrete consumer of the signed boundary. A trusted host registers a canonical built-in adapter profile, canonical source and allocation paths, the exact tracked-content digest, runtime generation, Git policy, and previously authorised version/audit invocation identities. NativeAuditOperation.request derives every repository read, workspace write and cleanup, and Git, Bubblewrap, and adapter execution effect; callers cannot omit one while retaining the same signed payload.

Admission completes before snapshot allocation or any process launch. The same host lease then compares the actual descriptor-held version and audit identities and rechecks custody, signature, expiry, revocation, and runtime state immediately before each process. Only tracked profile inputs enter the explicit host-owned allocation, and successful return means the unique owned workspace was removed. The receipt binds the request and policy digests, runtime generation, cleanup disposition, and the existing source-linked adapter result.

This API is opt-in and does not change the legacy CLI or generic argv adapter. The existing executor enforces tracked-input, per-file, output, and timeout bounds. Hosts must enforce any additional CPU, RAM, process, provider, or billing limit inside their retained state lease, or refuse the operation. This local consumer does not by itself claim remote publication, provider transport, production rollout, or completion of the wider tool-authority acceptance programme.

docs.title: Consumer integrations
docs.text: RigorFoundry publishes a composite GitHub Action and a pre-commit hook for adopter-owned audit gates. Both integrations are evidence-only surfaces: they can scan and evaluate an existing policy, but they cannot promote findings, apply remediation, edit source, create policy state, or infer private paths.

docs.title: GitHub Action
docs.text:
Pin the Action and every other workflow action to a complete commit SHA. The following revision is the provenance-hardened integration successor containing action.yml, .pre-commit-hooks.yaml, and the executable-provenance guards:

name: RigorFoundry

on:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: rigor-foundry-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  audit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Prepare explicit ignored output parent
        run: mkdir -p .rigor/reports
      - name: Run read-only evidence gate
        uses: anulum/RIGOR-FOUNDRY@cd7a06d6c2e6c1258006ade83aff5e94d5fb1cb2
        with:
          repository-root: .
          policy-path: rigor-foundry-policy.json
          report-path: .rigor/reports/report.json
          gate-report-path: .rigor/reports/gate.json
          mode: observe
          scope: full
          allow-native-audits: "false"

The output parents must already exist and both output files must be absent; the Action never overwrites a file or creates repository directories. An output inside the adopter worktree must be Git-ignored and untracked. The Action installs the exact checked-out source revision with Python 3.12.11, the hash-locked build requirements, and the hash-locked runtime requirements. The PEP 517 backend and all four of its build dependencies are exact requirements as well. Nested setup-python is itself pinned to a full commit. Inputs enter Bash only through quoted environment variables.

repository-root, repository-relative tracked policy-path, report-path, and gate-report-path are mandatory. mode accepts only observe, ratchet, or zero; scope accepts only staged or full. Ratchet and zero require an explicit maturity-path whose policy identity is already bound by the repository policy. An optional review-path replaces the policy-declared review ledger. A requested mode may strengthen the policy but cannot weaken it.

allow-native-audits defaults to false. Setting it to true is explicit consent only for policy-declared adapters running through the existing read-only sandbox; it grants no remediation authority. The Action contains no promote or --apply path.

docs.title: Pre-commit hook
docs.text:
Pin rev to the same complete commit SHA. The published hook defaults to the staged observe gate with rigor-foundry-policy.json. To retain an explicit gate artifact, configure the complete argument vector because adopter args replace, rather than extend, the manifest defaults:

minimum_pre_commit_version: 4.6.0
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/anulum/RIGOR-FOUNDRY
    rev: cd7a06d6c2e6c1258006ade83aff5e94d5fb1cb2
    hooks:
      - id: rigor-foundry
        entry: .rigor/rigor-venv/bin/rigor
        args:
          - gate
          - --root
          - .
          - --policy
          - rigor-foundry-policy.json
          - --mode
          - observe
          - --scope
          - staged
          - --output
          - .rigor/reports/pre-commit-gate.json

Create and ignore .rigor/reports before running the hook. The hook uses language: system deliberately: pre-commit's Python environment installer does not expose pip's --require-hashes contract. Install the pinned RigorFoundry checkout into .rigor/rigor-venv with its requirements/build.txt and requirements/runtime.txt hash locks, followed by pip install --no-build-isolation --no-deps CHECKOUT; then retain the explicit entry shown above. The manifest runs once serially without filenames and does not consent to native adapters. For ratchet or zero, replace the complete args list, select the stronger mode, and add --maturity PATH. Add --review PATH only when the review ledger is explicitly owned. Add --allow-native-audits only after reviewing the declared adapter commands and sandbox prerequisites.

docs.title: Verification boundary
docs.text:
Distribution CI builds and checks the wheel and source distribution, creates a separate real Git adopter under /tmp, bootstraps and commits its policy, runs the local composite Action against that repository, then makes pre-commit clone the source repository at the exact ${GITHUB_SHA} and execute the system hook through the hash-locked installed wheel. The workflow requires non-empty Action scan, Action gate, and pre-commit gate artifacts. Local author evidence repeats the Action shell and hook install against an external fixture; hosted CI remains the authoritative runner proof after an authorised push.

These integrations report policy evidence. They do not establish that every audit domain is implemented, that candidates are defects, that reviewed findings are resolved, or that the repository is production-ready.

docs.title: Inventory baselines and repository states
docs.text: These provisional module APIs connect the complete configured collector to independently retained before-images and the existing RepositoryState1 record. They inspect actual selected sources and file inputs. Their results remain observational data, with no owner-proof, task admission or effect permit.

docs.title: Explicit earlier inputs
docs.text:
inventory_baseline.InventoryBaseline1 uses schema 1.0 and object kind inventory-baseline. Its closed fields are baseline_id, project_id, domain_reference, registry_reference, roots and baseline_digest, alongside the two headers. Its digest binds every other field. Typed domain and registry references preserve their original identities and formats.

Each inline InventoryBaselineRoot retains its complete InventoryDomainRoot, git_head, files and directories:

  • A Git root has an explicit full commit and every original baseline file row, including blob or gitlink identities. No directory list is invented for Git.
  • An ignored or generated directory has no Git commit or object IDs. Its rows retain earlier observed byte identities and modes; all directories, including empty ones, remain explicit. Unsupported leaves and unknown classifications remain visible.

Roots and paths must be sorted and unique. File/directory collisions, a file used as a parent, missing directory parents and inconsistent history fields refuse. Parsing bounds root counts and aggregate root/file/directory references before retaining their contents. The source reader additionally applies its actual byte and JSON-depth ceilings. These are allocation limits, not execution or source-access authority.

docs.title: Actual baseline capture
docs.text:
repository_state_observations.capture_inventory_baseline calls the existing complete collector with the actual retained domain, registry and inventory contract, complete package/interpreter observation, trusted Git and explicit read budget. baselines supplies an InventoryGitBaseline for every and only declared Git root. baseline_id names the resulting source record.

The returned Git before-images come from those explicit commits. Directory before-images come from the actual agreeing directory reads at capture time. Persist and independently select this record before the subsequent change. Capturing the current directory again after an edit cannot recover its earlier state or prove generator lineage.

The fixed typed-source parser supports inventory-baseline format 1.0. Only the inventory producer's format domain accepts that source kind. As with other retained sources, the host independently selects the exact path, typed reference and original raw SHA-256 before opening RetainedContextSource. A valid self-digest alone establishes no historical authenticity or right to access the named files.

docs.title: Actual repository-state observation
docs.text:
repository_state_observations.observe_repository_state receives that actual baseline_source and the same host-selected capture inputs. The inventory contract must explicitly include the selected baseline format. The observer captures every current declared root and compares the complete before/current root selection, project, domain and registry identities. Each Git before-image must reproduce the selected commit's actual original blobs.

root_id selects the declared Git root whose baseline/head/tree fields name the returned RepositoryState1. It never filters the remaining roots. Missing or directory-only selections refuse. Selecting another Git root preserves the same complete input domain and independent inventory/index/worktree identities.

The observer derives and retains:

  • The full explicit baseline identity, including earlier directory preimages.
  • Every current index stage across all Git roots.
  • Every current file row, directory topology and actual Git head/tree/status and executable provenance.
  • Actual nonignored untracked paths and their current rows.
  • Complete current generated-directory observations and the configured domain.

Deleted Git files retain their original baseline rows alongside explicit current deletions. Removed directory files and directories remain in the independently retained before-images. Current observations cannot rewrite their history. Unknown language/role and unsupported entries participate in the state; they do not become evidence of complete maintained-language qualification.

RepositoryStateObservation returns state, the full original inputs, the retained baseline and source_snapshot_digest. The last value binds the actual configured-source selection, retained baseline reference/lifetime and derived state, plus the device/inode of each captured directory root. Replacing a directory with equal bytes can preserve its content state while changing this source-snapshot identity. A final baseline read rejects an edit during the Git/file observation, even if all current-root reads themselves completed successfully.

Domain or registry changes require explicit history reconciliation. This observer refuses mismatches instead of dropping old roots, replacing an earlier baseline with current bytes, or assuming an empty history.

Agreement across these bounded observations is not an atomic cross-root snapshot or uninterrupted physical-root lease. Required host-root selection, generator provenance/reproducibility, revocation, authenticated inventory/fact/task owners and runtime admission retain their separate contracts. These APIs change neither frozen package-root exports nor the installed CLI.

docs.title: Configured inventory domains
docs.text:
The provisional inventory_domain.InventoryDomain1 records the complete declared roots and path-classification rules for one project. It uses schema 1.0, object kind inventory-domain, a domain/project ID, sorted root/rule arrays and a digest over all other fields. Its typed source reference is supported by the existing fixed source parser and retained source lease.

Each inline root contains its ID, canonical monorepo-relative path and source kind: git, ignored or generated. Parsing a declaration does not open or enrol any of those roots. Root IDs and paths are unique; every rule references a declared root. Explicit source, rule and reference ceilings apply before child parsing.

An inline classification rule contains root_id, field, selector_kind, selector and value. Languages permit literal exact paths and lowercase suffix selectors. Roles permit exact paths and whole-component prefix selectors. Role values are source, test, tool, fixture, example, benchmark, generator, configuration and documentation. Language values are explicit identifiers; declaring one does not qualify its language adapter or verify content syntax. Glob, regex, callback and loader selectors are absent.

inventory_classification.classify_repository_file_inputs preserves every baseline/current file input. An exact path takes precedence. Otherwise the longest matching lowercase filename suffix selects the language, and the longest whole-component prefix selects the role. Unmatched fields stay null. Unsupported and gitlink rows remain unknown; their independent byte/root owners cannot be replaced by a filename label. Deleted paths remain represented with their before identities available.

docs.title: Actual selected Git-root observations
docs.text:
inventory_source_observations.observe_classified_git_root uses actual borrowed domain, registry and inventory-contract source leases, a host-selected monorepo root, a prior complete package/interpreter observation, an actual Git runner and explicit read budgets. It does not accept a request-appointed parser or implementation loader.

The function compares every declared project root with the actual contract root set, project/group ownership, canonical path and configured-scope digest. The contract must describe the fixed builtin.maintained-inventory.v1 implementation and support the actual selected domain and registry formats. Legacy descriptive inventory contracts remain parseable; omitting the domain format cannot authorise this new observer. The actual installed package and interpreter observation is checked before and after the file capture.

The selected Git root is read through the actual file-input API, then classified. Sources are revalidated at closure, and the host-root pathname must retain its original directory identity. The result retains the domain, registry and contract references, complete selected-root input data and a source-selection snapshot.

This observes one Git root. It does not capture the declaration's other roots, enumerate ignored/generated directories, establish complete maintained inventory, authenticate a task/fact context or issue an owner/admission proof. All declared roots remain bound by the domain reference; a complete owning consumer must collect and verify them independently. Existing source-access, whole-host resource, runtime, revocation and effect guards remain required.

Configured inventory inputs composes the shared retained-source selection with every declared Git and directory root. It preserves original observations and explicit nested namespace ownership; its declared-root completeness does not establish host admission or history.

docs.title: Jupyter notebook analysis
docs.text: RigorFoundry inspects tracked .ipynb files without importing Jupyter, starting a kernel, executing a code cell, or modifying the audited checkout. The scanner consumes only the bounded UTF-8 blob captured by the normal Git inventory.

docs.title: Supported boundary
docs.text:
The notebook must use nbformat 4 and declare one unambiguous python or python3 language through metadata.language_info.name and/or metadata.kernelspec.language. Code-cell source may be either the standard string form or an array of strings. Markdown and raw cells are retained in the blob identity but are not interpreted as Python.

Each code cell is parsed independently with the supported Python AST. The following existing rule families are applicable:

  • application security, reliability, and data privacy for every Python cell;
  • operations and observability when the notebook is under a configured production source root;
  • scientific, performance, and AST-backed test-authenticity rules when the notebook is under a configured test root.

Architecture, package API, import-graph, and module-ownership rules are not applied to synthetic notebook cells because a cell is not a Python module. The older repository-wide textual test-authenticity layer remains separate and may still identify suppression syntax in any tracked UTF-8 text, including raw notebook JSON; those text candidates are not produced by the cell-AST bridge.

docs.title: Exact anchors and evidence
docs.text: Candidate locations are translated from the cell's logical Python line back to the physical JSON string token or tokens in the exact tracked notebook blob. String-array fragments that jointly form one Python line produce one inclusive notebook line span. A single JSON string containing escaped newlines remains anchored to that exact physical JSON line. Evidence contains only blob/span digests, the cell index, and logical source-line range; raw cell source is not copied into the report.

docs.title: Fail-closed states
docs.text:
GV005-unscanned-jupyter-notebook is emitted when JSON is malformed, keys are duplicated, nesting or cell-count bounds are exceeded, nbformat is unsupported, the language is missing/conflicting/non-Python, a code-cell source shape is invalid, or a declared Python cell cannot be parsed. Valid cells in a notebook remain independently reviewable, but the GV005 candidate prevents an incomplete notebook from looking clean.

The Git inventory's existing 8 MiB text bound remains authoritative. Oversize, binary, non-UTF-8, symlink, or otherwise unreadable tracked notebooks receive the existing GV002-unscanned-tracked-code candidate. Neither failure path falls back to kernel execution or reads notebook outputs as executable code.

docs.title: Maintained inventory and source facts
docs.text: These provisional module APIs connect the actual baseline/state observer and fixed task/registry owners to complete maintained surface records and source-verified condition facts. They are called by trusted host composition with actual retained sources and fixed owner entries.

docs.title: Complete maintained scope
docs.text:
maintained_surface.MaintainedSurface1 and maintained_inventory.MaintainedInventory1 use schema 1.0. A surface retains its exact root-relative path, declared role/language, effective byte digest, nullable earlier byte digest and inventory proof. The enclosing inventory binds project/registry identities, independently derived repository/baseline digests, every declared root, every maintained surface, change/completeness proofs and its final digest. Parsing these records verifies integrity and relationships; it does not authenticate their issuer or their physical sources.

Roots are sorted and unique. Surfaces are sorted by (root_id, relative_path) with no duplicate root/path. Empty roots remain declared. Before/current unions retain deleted files and both sides of a move. Overlapping configured roots retain their own complete surface observations; selecting a task root does not discard other roots. All actual Git index stages and directory topology remain bound by the independent repository state and original captures.

The change proof and every surface proof bind the independent repository-state subject. The completeness proof binds the independently retained baseline. Both proofs must name the same inventory owner, contract and snapshot. Their subjects precede the enclosing inventory digest, so there is no digest cycle. Byte/count/depth and aggregate root/surface/proof budgets remain explicit.

docs.title: Actual fixed inventory owner
docs.text:
inventory_source_owner.InventorySourceOwner receives the host-selected physical monorepo root, actual retained domain/registry/inventory-contract/ baseline/repository-state sources, complete package/interpreter observation, trusted Git runner and read budget. Persist and independently select a repository-state record obtained through the actual observer before creating this entry. The owner compares that retained state with freshly observed roots.

observe() returns OwnedMaintainedInventory: the full inventory, independently generated change/completeness observations and proofs, and the full original RepositoryStateObservation. verify(value) recomputes the actual selected sources, root state and complete inventory; matching caller metadata alone cannot substitute for the original entry. Another entry has another snapshot identity. close() revalidates actual state and closes the entry, while the host retains ownership of the borrowed source leases.

Current regular-file bytes and raw symlink target bytes retain their actual identities. A deleted file uses its explicitly retained earlier bytes, never invented current content. Staged divergence participates in changed paths even when worktree bytes equal the baseline. Unknown language/role, unsupported byte history, an unresolved merge index or a newly staged file with no remaining worktree/baseline bytes holds the ready inventory. Such inputs remain present in the original complete captures; they are never silently filtered. A gitlink commit identity does not become a fabricated file-content digest.

Declared path classifications are distinct from content-language validation, generator lineage and native toolchain acceptance. The owner verifies the full selected declared domain; enclosing host policy still owns which roots must be declared and the right to read them. Agreeing bounded reads do not establish an atomic snapshot, uninterrupted physical-root lease or effect permission.

docs.title: Closed fact data
docs.text:
fact_context.FactObservation1 retains an exact dotted reference, explicit state/value, independent subject, nullable provenance and final digest. Known null and empty arrays remain observed values. Authoritative absence requires a matching proof; unknown requires null value and null provenance. Missing an exact reference never manufactures absence for it or descendants. Finite scalar identities preserve Boolean/number distinctions.

FactContext1 binds the independent task identity, current registry generation and digest, complete inventory digest, sorted unique producer proofs and sorted unique observations. Every nonunknown observation must belong to its selected proof set. Contradictory observed parent/child references refuse. Structural parsing grants no producer authentication.

docs.title: Source-verified evaluation
docs.text:
source_fact_context.observe_source_fact_context accepts only actual fixed TaskRegistrySourceOwners and InventorySourceOwner entries, an actor/root and explicit budget. It derives the original seven task, eight registry and five inventory facts from those owners. Missing producer domains, conflicting project/ root/registry selections or overlapping owner identities refuse. Complete task/registry root bindings must match every actual inventory root, physical path, owning group and configured-domain digest. Matching root labels alone cannot substitute another selected path or scope. Each actual owner revalidates its original observations before the context is returned.

verify_source_fact_context compares a complete supplied context with actual new source-owner observations. evaluate_source_fact_condition performs that verification before and after existing ConditionExpression1.1 tri-state evaluation. It returns ConditionTruth.TRUE, FALSE or UNKNOWN; implicit Boolean conversion remains forbidden. Missing facts stay unknown, invalid known operand domains refuse, and no decisive sibling excuses incomplete maintained scope.

Source identity verification does not authenticate the initiating user, event, claim or audit request. These APIs do not implement enclosing task admission, selected rule generation, runtime revocation/effects or native permission. Their new result models do not expand the fixed retained-source parser table, frozen package-root exports or installed CLI.

The task-context source composer now consumes these verified facts and complete inventory with the original general task and explicit event. It additionally supports optional actual retained remediation sources; the separate work-source adapters enrol only their fixed supported source formats. The task composer issues no claim proof or operational permission.

docs.title: Offline evidence verification
docs.text:
rigor verify is the stable free verification boundary for signed RigorFoundry evidence. It reads only caller-supplied local files. It contains no network client, service discovery, telemetry, fleet authority, or paid service dependency.

rigor verify \
  --bundle evidence-bundle.json \
  --trust-policy trust-policy.json \
  --at 2026-07-20T12:00:00Z \
  --output verification-result.json

--at is mandatory and must be UTC. An explicit evaluation time makes expiry and revocation results replayable instead of depending on an ambient clock. Without --output, the result is written to stdout. Output creation is exclusive and never overwrites an existing path.

The command returns:

  • 0 only when every bundle entry is verified;
  • 1 for a parseable result containing invalid, stale, or unavailable evidence;
  • 2 for malformed, unsafe, oversized, or unsupported input.

docs.title: Caller-selected trust
docs.text:
The trust policy is a separate input, not part of the untrusted evidence bundle. Replacing the bundle therefore cannot silently replace its trusted keys. Policy schema 1.0 binds each unique Ed25519 key and public-key digest to valid_from, valid_until, and an optional revoked_at instant. Duplicate key IDs and public-key aliases are rejected.

Verification distinguishes:

  • unknown, not-yet-valid, and revoked keys as invalid;
  • an expired key as stale evidence;
  • a key that was not active at the evidence signing time as invalid.

Report, review, and model-alias signatures bind a signing time. The existing StandardPack signature has no signing-time field, so pack verification proves the native signature under a key active at the explicit evaluation time; it does not reconstruct historical key status.

docs.title: Bundle records
docs.text:
Bundle schema 1.0 contains a sorted, unique set of evidence entries. Every available entry embeds its strict production protocol document and exact digest. Every unavailable entry preserves the expected digest and a non-empty reason without inventing document bytes.

Supported kinds are:

Kind Verification contract audit-report Reparse the complete report and every nested digest, then verify a time-bounded signature in rigor-foundry.audit-report.v1. review Reparse the review and reviewer attestation, bind the review digest and decision, and verify the existing reviewer-attestation domain and expiry. standard-pack Reparse the pack, controls, native PackSignature, payload digest, and the existing standard-pack domain. model-aliases Reparse provider, exact-model, family, operator, and run identities; recompute transitive alias collapse; then verify rigor-foundry.model-aliases.v1.

The review decision mapping is fixed: valid to pass, invalid to fail, accepted-boundary to accepted-risk, and needs-evidence to needs-evidence. Contradictory signed decisions are invalid.

Report and model-alias envelopes sign a canonical payload digest containing the schema, evidence kind, Ed25519 algorithm, protocol domain, key ID, exact artifact digest, signing time, and expiry. A signature from another domain cannot be relabelled or replayed.

The aggregate report is itself content-addressed. It binds the evaluation time, selected trust-policy digest, input bundle digest, ordered per-evidence results, bounded details, aggregate status, and report digest. Status precedence is invalid, stale, unavailable, then verified; partial evidence can never be upgraded.

docs.title: Input boundary
docs.text: Bundle and trust-policy inputs must be single-link regular files opened with no-follow semantics. Symbolic links, hard links, concurrent identity changes, invalid UTF-8 or JSON, and documents above 16 MiB fail closed. This is a local file-verification boundary, not a repository mutation command.

docs.title: Assurance boundary
docs.text:
A verified result proves only that the supplied bytes satisfy the declared schemas, digests, signatures, key lifecycle, expiry, review binding, and alias relations under the caller-selected trust policy. It does not prove:

  • that a report is current for a live repository or that its candidates are defect verdicts;
  • that the selected trust policy is authoritative for another organisation;
  • model independence beyond the explicit correlation declarations;
  • remediation success, fleet admission, regulatory conformity, or universal software safety.

Assurance campaigns, enforcement, fleet views, and remediation authority stay outside this free verification path.

docs.title: Operations and observability rules
docs.text: Rule-pack rigor-foundry/1.14.0 adds the bounded operations category (prefix OP). Findings are anchored needs-evidence candidates, not proof of an outage, secret disclosure, or inadequate observability.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rule Signal Confidence OP001-print-in-library-code tracked Python library code calls builtin print outside a conventional command surface medium OP002-credential-in-log-call an import-bound standard-library logging call directly receives a credential-named expression high

Both rules require tracked UTF-8 Python below an exact policy source root and exclude test paths. OP001 also excludes top-level tools, scripts, and bin roots plus cli.py, __main__.py, and *_cli.py modules. It recognises local or module shadowing of print and separately detects explicit builtins.print. Reviewers should replace incidental process output with a return value or structured logger, or prove the module is an intentional command boundary.

OP002 resolves explicit logging imports, getLogger aliases, assigned logger instances, and chained logging.getLogger(...).method(...) calls for the standard debug/info/warning/error/critical/exception/log methods. Only variable or attribute names that identify credential material trigger; message labels, arbitrary payloads, custom logging frameworks, and names ending in metadata descriptors such as hash, digest, id, or path do not. Reviewers must remove or redact the value and inspect captured output at the real logging boundary.

Syntax-invalid Python yields no OP candidate because the existing authenticity rule owns parse failure. Evidence contains exact tracked-blob and line/file digests without copying source or credential values. Absence of OP002 is not proof that logs contain no secrets; dynamic values and unsupported logging frameworks require separate evidence.

The family contributes a portable control to operations-and-observability. Both rules enter maturity probation and cannot drive enforcement until adjudicated cross-repository precision and reviewer-effort evidence exists.

docs.title: Performance and reproducibility rules
docs.text: Rule-pack rigor-foundry/1.15.0 adds the bounded performance category (prefix PR). Findings are anchored needs-evidence candidates, not proof that a test is flaky, slow, or incorrect.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rule Signal Confidence PR001-wall-clock-in-test an import-bound time.time() or datetime.now() call is evaluated by a Python test assertion without recognised local clock control high

PR001 resolves explicit module and direct imports of time.time and datetime.datetime.now. It groups all uncontrolled clock reads in one test function into one candidate anchored at the first call. Calls outside an assertion, monotonic elapsed-time measurements, custom clocks, production code, and unsupported wrappers are outside this deliberately narrow signal.

The rule recognises a freezer test fixture, import-bound freezegun.freeze_time and time_machine.travel decorators or context managers, and a preceding straight-line monkeypatch.setattr of the exact imported module/class binding. A patch inside a conditional branch does not suppress a later assertion outside that branch. monkeypatch.undo() restores candidate detection. Directly imported callables remain candidates when only their source module is patched because the copied local binding is unchanged. Arbitrary fixtures, string suffixes, custom wrappers, and production-module patches are not inferred as clock control.

Only tracked UTF-8 .py files classified as tests by repository policy or test naming are parsed. Syntax-invalid Python yields no PR candidate because the existing unparseable-test authenticity rule owns that condition. Evidence contains exact tracked-blob and line/file digests plus bounded API identifiers; it never copies assertion source.

Reviewers should inject a clock, freeze the exact assertion boundary, or prove that the live-clock check has a bounded timing contract resilient to wall-clock adjustment and scheduler delay. A candidate may be adjudicated invalid or an accepted boundary when that evidence is retained.

The family contributes a portable control to performance-and-reproducibility. PR001 enters maturity probation and cannot drive enforcement until adjudicated cross-repository precision and reviewer-effort evidence exists.

docs.title: Permit anchor verification and recovery evidence
docs.text: PermitLedgerAnchorStoreV2 binds an owner-only anchor file to complete permit ledger and effect journal histories. RecoveryEvidenceStoreV2 publishes exact canonical recovery objects under their SHA-256 filenames. These provisional module-level Python APIs retain the V2.4 anchor and V2.1 journal recovery wires. They add no stable CLI command or package-level 1.0 compatibility promise.

docs.title: Selected files and ordinary verification
docs.text:
The caller supplies absolute paths beneath existing no-follow directories owned by the effective UID with mode 0700. Anchor and evidence objects must be regular, single-link, owner-owned files with mode 0600. An ordinary fixture demonstrates these storage checks; it does not establish protected host selection, authenticate a supervisor, or grant an effect permission.

Initialise a new empty ledger and journal before creating their anchor:

from pathlib import Path

from rigor_foundry.effect_journal_v2 import EffectJournalStoreV2
from rigor_foundry.permit_anchor_store_v2 import PermitLedgerAnchorStoreV2
from rigor_foundry.permit_consumption_ledger_v2 import ConsumedPermitLedgerV2
from rigor_foundry.recovery_evidence_store_v2 import RecoveryEvidenceStoreV2

# The caller has already provisioned custody and custody/evidence at mode 0700.
custody = Path("/srv/rigor/custody")
ledger = ConsumedPermitLedgerV2(custody / "consumed.bin")
journal = EffectJournalStoreV2(custody / "effect.journal")
anchor = PermitLedgerAnchorStoreV2(custody / "anchor.bin")
evidence = RecoveryEvidenceStoreV2(custody / "evidence", 64, 1_000_000)
ledger.initialize()
journal.initialize()
initial = anchor.initialize(ledger=ledger, journal=journal, max_journal_bytes=1_000_000)
selected = anchor.current(
    ledger=ledger,
    journal=journal,
    evidence=evidence,
    selected_journal_identity=initial.journal_identity,
    max_journal_bytes=1_000_000,
)
assert selected.ledger_record_count == 0

Initialisation creates the anchor exclusively and fsyncs its bytes and parent; an existing file refuses replacement. current() holds locks in anchor → ledger → journal order, validates the complete retained prefix, rechecks file custody, and returns the verified selection and journal replay state. The host supplies the expected journal identity and finite byte budget independently.

docs.title: Anchor wire and recovery commitments
docs.text:
The magic is RIGOR-PERMIT-ANCHOR-V2.4\n; each complete record is 200 bytes with big-endian layout >B3xQ32s32sQQQI32s32s32s. Reserved bytes are zero. The chain head is SHA-256 of the previous head plus the first 168 record bytes.

Kind Verified meaning 0 Genesis, ordinary consumption bound to exactly one matching final operation intent, or a journal-only advance that admits no operation intent. 1 Final-tail recovery commitment; preserves the prior ledger and journal selections and resolves one exact root/child intent chain. 2 Complete ledger suffix adoption, bound to immutable evidence, exact record arrays, selected file identities and the consumed UUID commitment. 3 Newly honoured closure, naming the last new closure frame for an already selected operation.

Only a sole final partial or invalid complete record after a valid initial prefix can be classified as tail damage. First/interior damage refuses. Classification does not authorise truncation. Ordinary reads refuse damaged tails, unresolved selected recovery intents, ledger suffixes requiring adoption, missing evidence, and orphan audit frames. A complete unanchored audit or closure remains inert.

The tail scanner verifies the initial record against the ledger, journal and anchor genesis values before scanning successors. Each successor therefore inherits an already verified selection.

The three closed evidence domains are:

  • rigor.permit-anchor-final-recovery.v2.4
  • rigor.permit-anchor-recovery.v2.4
  • rigor.effect-journal-tail-recovery.v2.1

Public validators in recovery_evidence_schema_v2 produce exact PCS-CANON-1 bytes. They reject extra or missing fields, duplicate keys, noncanonical JSON, path/time/base64 aliases, unsafe JSON integers, and inconsistent captured lengths or digests. Grammar-valid operator identities and proof references are data; they do not authenticate an operator.

docs.title: Immutable evidence custody
docs.text:
publish(data) validates the entire object, checks count and aggregate byte budgets, writes and fsyncs exact bytes, and returns their SHA-256 digest. Publishing identical bytes is idempotent. Journal intent publication uses Linux renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) on a staged object; syscall refusal fails closed and clears staging. Anchor-domain objects use exclusive digest-file creation; an interrupted write can leave an invalid object that blocks subsequent reads.

read(digest) and scan() validate every published object and the complete bounded directory enumeration. Staging remnants confer no authority but count toward the entry budget. Symlinks, additional hard links, substituted paths, changed bytes and special files refuse. Writerless FIFOs are opened nonblocking and rejected by the regular-file custody check.

Callers retain their selected chain locks while consulting evidence. The store checks canonical bytes and custody; the anchor prefix verifier separately checks semantic relationships to the selected chains. The destructive recovery and adoption operators require an authenticated supervisor integration and are not provided by these APIs.

The public journal intent verifier also rechecks each supplied map key against the SHA-256 of its exact object bytes before filtering domains or file identities. A caller cannot introduce a digest alias by supplying an in-memory object map.

This storage implementation uses POSIX locks and Linux no-replace publication. It has no Rust, Go, TypeScript or Windows runtime counterpart. Existing adapter benchmarks measure another surface and make no performance claim about these storage operations.

docs.title: Permit consumption ledger
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.permit_consumption_ledger_v2.ConsumedPermitLedgerV2 records consumed permit UUIDs in a local file. It rejects replay across both the permit and optional single-use UUID fields, verifies the complete hash chain, and fsyncs each complete append before returning its head.

This module-level Python API supplies storage mechanics. The consuming host separately verifies signatures, actual expiry, authority, selection and protected anchors. A digest or parsed record grants no effect permission, and this API does not dispatch a handler or enrol a service account. The stable CLI and package-level compatibility contract are unchanged.

docs.title: File and wire contract
docs.text:
The caller selects an absolute path under an existing parent owned by the current service UID with mode 0700. An existing ledger must be a regular, single-link file owned by that UID with mode 0600. Paths are opened through no-follow directory descriptors; symlinks, hard links, wrong modes, torn tails, invalid complete rows and mismatched selected prefixes refuse.

The fixed header is RIGOR-PERMIT-LEDGER-V2.2\n. Complete records use the big-endian layout >B3x16s16s32sQI32s, containing a kind, zero padding, two UUIDs, digest, positive UTC epoch microseconds, metadata and the previous chain head. The next head is SHA-256 of the previous head followed by the record bytes excluding their final previous-head field. Consumption uses kind zero and metadata zero; explicit recovery uses kind one and records the removed tail's SHA-256 and length. Reserved UUIDs, an all-zero digest and nonzero padding refuse.

expires_at is retained metadata. This storage layer checks its wire range, not whether a signed permit is currently valid. The caller must make that authority decision before requesting consumption.

docs.title: Public operations
docs.text:
Operation Behaviour initialize() Exclusively create and fsync a new ledger and its parent; never replace an existing file. consume(...) Verify all history, refuse either previously consumed UUID, append and fsync one complete row. verify_anchor(...) Verify a caller-supplied prefix against all current records and return current count and head. verify_anchor_with_identity(...) Return that result and the same locked file's path digest, device and inode. locked_snapshot(...) Retain the actual lock while exposing all verified records; recheck custody on exit. locked_admission(...) Issue one append lease only when the complete current tail equals the selected count and head. recover_torn_tail(...) Explicitly remove only an incomplete tail after validating all complete history, then fsync an audited recovery row.

A snapshot may extend an older valid selected prefix. An admission lease requires the exact current tail and refuses an unanchored suffix. Consumption through an issued lease rechecks actual file custody and complete history, including same-size changes, immediately before appending. Each lease permits one append attempt and belongs to its original process. Closing the context or forking refuses later use; ordinary descriptor-number reuse cannot revive it. Directly constructing a lease does not issue one. Python copy, deep-copy and pickle operations also refuse for these descriptor leases.

An I/O failure or final custody refusal is not a rollback promise. A complete consumption is retained even if a later handler fails. The qualified host must retain its selection and anchor locks through ledger, journal and anchor fsync, and reconcile failures using its separately authorised recovery procedure.

docs.title: Local storage example
docs.text:
This example exercises a disposable file. Its initial head is a storage result, not a protected host selection or a signed permission.

from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from uuid import uuid4

from rigor_foundry.permit_consumption_ledger_v2 import ConsumedPermitLedgerV2

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    parent = Path(directory)
    parent.chmod(0o700)
    ledger = ConsumedPermitLedgerV2(parent / "consumed.bin")
    initial = ledger.initialize()
    with ledger.locked_admission(
        selected_count=0, selected_head_digest=initial
    ) as transaction:
        record = transaction.consume(
            permit_id=str(uuid4()),
            single_use_id=str(uuid4()),
            permit_digest="a" * 64,
            expires_at=datetime.now(UTC).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z"),
        )
    assert ledger.verify_anchor(
        record_count=1, head_digest=record.head_digest
    ) == (1, record.head_digest)

The example's digest and timestamp are ordinary storage inputs. A real consumer supplies the digest and expiry from its independently verified permit.

docs.title: Ownership and qualification
docs.text:
permit_consumption_ledger_v2 owns file locking, actual snapshots, append-lease lifetime and explicit recovery. _permit_ledger_records_v2 owns the fixed binary wire, UUID/time validation, complete replay and immutable record carriers. _permit_ledger_storage_io_v2 owns descriptor identity, owner checks and bounded complete reads/writes. Public ledger workflows exercise both private owners.

The dedicated tests cover durable replay, concurrent consumers, both UUID fields, actual stored corruption, modes and links, selected prefixes, stale and inherited leases, descriptor reuse and explicit torn-tail recovery. Ordinary user-owned fixtures qualify these mechanics; they do not qualify a protected signer, deployment, native handler or effect-admission chain.

docs.title: Policy source bytes
docs.text:
The provisional Python APIs read supplied local policy inputs and verify their exact byte coordinates. Every input transaction supplies its allocation limits. The three record kinds policy-read-budget, source-span and source-region use schema 1.0, closed fields and digests that include their kind and version.

from pathlib import Path

from rigor_foundry.policy_read_budget import PolicyReadBudget1
from rigor_foundry.policy_source_reads import read_policy_document

budget = PolicyReadBudget1.build(
    max_document_bytes=65_536,
    max_source_bytes=1_048_576,
    max_total_source_bytes=4_194_304,
    max_sources=32,
    max_rules=256,
    max_references=2_048,
    max_depth=16,
)
document = read_policy_document(Path("rules.json"), budget=budget)

The reader rejects duplicate JSON keys, nonfinite numbers, invalid UTF8, unpaired escaped surrogates, excessive nesting and oversized files. It uses the existing stable single-link regular-file reader without following symlinks. Nesting is checked before recursive JSON decoding. Numeric byte ceilings also bound reading work; they do not merely limit retained buffering.

The fixed implementation ceilings are:
