Budget field Maximum max_document_bytes 8 MiB max_source_bytes 8 MiB max_total_source_bytes 64 MiB max_sources 4,096 max_rules 16,384 max_references 65,536 max_depth 32

All seven fields are explicit positive integers; Booleans are refused. read_policy_source_payloads(paths, budget=budget) reads a complete supplied source-ID/path mapping in source-ID order. It enforces the source count, individual file bytes and combined payload bytes before returning any result. An empty source remains a member of the supplied cohort.

policy_source_spans.SourceSpan1 binds a nonempty half-open byte interval [start_byte, end_byte) and its raw SHA-256. Its build method uses actual bytes; from_dict checks structural identity; verify(payload) additionally checks bounds and content. UTF8 character offsets and normalized newlines cannot substitute for original source bytes. verify_policy_source_spans(paths, spans, budget=budget) performs the bounded file reads and checks every supplied span, retaining selection order.

policy_source_regions.SourceRegion1 records an interval's declared normative, context, nonnormative, protected or unresolved disposition, exact rule/decision IDs and reason code. verify_policy_source_regions(paths, regions, budget=budget) checks byte digests and requires a complete, ordered partition of every supplied source. Missing beginnings or tails, gaps, overlap, reordered regions and unresolved source IDs are refused. Normative regions require rule IDs. Rule and decision ID arrays are sorted and unique. Each region consumes one source reference plus its rule and decision links; distinct referenced rule IDs also consume the rule budget.

A valid partition proves byte accounting for the supplied cohort. It does not prove that all governing sources were supplied, that extracted rules have the correct meaning, that referenced rules/decisions have been accepted, or that protected content may be read. Those checks belong to the corpus and installed host owners. Protected and unresolved dispositions remain explicit data after byte verification; neither becomes a ready-boot or effect grant.

The retained source universe connects these original span and region models to a complete fixed host-selected source cohort. It retains actual metadata and raw descriptors through use/closure, verifies original native pins and complete discovery snapshots, and consumes partitions over those same held bytes. Held/excluded sources remain explicit; no locator becomes a path and no byte check accepts extraction meaning.

Rule declarations and original components retain these original spans and conditions in explicit scope, semantic-decision and atomic-rule records. Their parsers preserve declaration integrity; actual source and semantic acceptance remain separate.

docs.title: Polyglot capability matrix
docs.text: RigorFoundry is not a Python-only tool, and it does not claim uniform semantic depth across languages. It scans thirteen languages at deliberately different depths. This matrix states, per language, which analysis techniques the scanner actually applies, so an adopter can see exactly what a green scan does and does not establish. It is derived from the live language-capability registry, so it cannot drift from the scanner's behaviour.

docs.title: Three technique classes
docs.text:
• AST / semantic controls — the scanner parses the language's source into an abstract syntax tree and reasons over it. This backs the test-authenticity rules (TA001–TA011) and the Python import-graph architecture rules (AR001–AR004, AR006). It is currently Python only.
  • Structural / textual heuristics — responsibility-size ownership (GF001), missing-test-owner ownership (AR005 for Python, AR008 for the polyglot suffixes), and relative dependency-graph resolution. These apply across the polyglot surface without parsing a full AST.
  • Native adapters — third-party tools (for example Semgrep for application-security) wired through a policy adapter profile. They are opt-in per repository policy and only run once their executable passes the trusted-executable provenance gate; they are not a per-language default.

docs.title: Matrix
docs.text:
Language AST / semantic Size (GF001) Ownership Dependency graph Structural python ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ c / c++ ✅† ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ javascript ✅† ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ typescript ✅† ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ rust ✅† ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ julia ✅† ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ go ✅† ✅ ✅ — ✅ lean — ✅ ✅ — ✅ mojo — ✅ ✅ — ✅ systemverilog — ✅ ✅ — ✅ verilog — ✅ ✅ — ✅ shell ✅† ✅ — — ✅ yaml — — — — —

✅ marks an applied technique; — marks one the scanner does not apply to that language today. † marks the native AST/semantic analysis for JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Rust, C/C++, Julia, and Shell, which is implemented through tree-sitter parsers but requires the optional native extra (pip install rigor-foundry[native]); without the extra a deployment degrades to the structural controls for those languages. YAML is scope-scannable data only — it participates in the tracked-content scope rule but carries no size, ownership, or dependency control. Go, Lean, Mojo, and the hardware-description languages are owned for size and ownership but have no native dependency-family parser yet.

docs.title: Reading a scan honestly
docs.text: A green scan means the applied techniques found no candidate — not that the language was analysed as deeply as Python. JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Rust, C/C++, Julia, and Shell now have a native AST pass (via the native extra); the remaining languages (Lean, Mojo, the hardware-description languages, and YAML) run only their structural or scope controls, so semantic defects that only an AST pass would surface are out of scope for them, guided by adopter evidence.

docs.title: Programmatic access
docs.text:
from rigor_foundry.polyglot_capability_matrix import capability_matrix

matrix = capability_matrix()
row = matrix.row("typescript")
row.ast_semantic_controls        # False — no AST pass yet
row.dependency_graph_controls    # True  — relative imports are resolved

The matrix is content-addressed (matrix_digest) and reachable via submodule import (rigor_foundry.polyglot_capability_matrix).

docs.title: Reliability rules
docs.text: Rule-pack rigor-foundry/1.8.0 adds a bounded reliability category (prefix RL) of high-precision, AST-backed rules over tracked Python. Like every RigorFoundry rule, each RL finding is an anchored needs-evidence candidate, never a verdict: it marks a real reliability-relevant surface for review, not a proven defect. The rules are deliberately narrow to keep false positives low; breadth is not an acceptance metric.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rule Signal Confidence RL001-bare-except a bare except: handler with no exception type high RL002-mutable-default-argument a function default that constructs a fresh list, dict, or set high

Both rules match on the Python AST, not on text. RL001 flags an except handler whose type is absent, which catches every exception — including SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt — and so hides real failures and blocks interruption; a typed handler such as except ValueError: is not flagged. RL002 flags a default argument that is a [...], {...}, or {…} literal, or an empty list(), dict(), or set() constructor call: such a default is created once and shared across every call, so state leaks between invocations. An immutable default (None, a number, a string, a tuple), a constructor call with arguments (list([0]), dict(a=1)), a non-builtin call (make()), and an attribute call (ns.factory()) are deliberately not flagged.

Each candidate carries a repository-tree anchor (path, line, content SHA-256), a neutral rationale, and a concrete verification procedure — for RL001, catch the specific exception types the block can actually handle or re-raise after recording context; for RL002, default the parameter to None and construct the container inside the function body, or confirm the shared instance is genuinely intended.

docs.title: Precision and applicability
docs.text: Because the rules match on the AST, a mention inside a string or comment is not flagged, and hardened equivalents are ignored by construction. The category applies to every tracked Python file, because a reliability defect is not test-only. It contributes a portable control toward the reliability-and-concurrency audit domain over the tracked Python surface.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text: False-positive calibration against real repositories is deliberately separate work: these rules ship with safe-and-vulnerable fixtures and precise AST matching, but adjudicated false-positive and reviewer-effort evidence across adopter repositories is the maturity-lifecycle step that promotes a rule from candidate breadth to calibrated enforcement.

docs.title: Remediation execution authority and ledger
docs.text: An approved remediation plan is advisory until it is both explicitly authorised and actually executed. RigorFoundry separates those two acts. The remediation_authority module grants bounded, independent authority to execute an exact approved plan; the remediation_executor module records an attested execution ledger against that authority. Neither module runs a procedure, spawns a process, or mutates a repository — execution happens elsewhere, under the authority, and its attested outcome is only validated and content-addressed here.

docs.title: Execution authority
docs.text:
An ExecutionAuthority binds an independently approved RemediationPlan to an ExecutionBudget and an explicit grant:

  • Approved plan only. Authority requires a plan in the approved state with an independent approval; an advisory plan cannot be authorised.
  • Author excluded. The grantor is never the plan's author, so authoring a plan never authorises its own execution.
  • Bounded validity. The grant has a UTC window (granted_at before expires_at) and a mode: observe authorises a non-mutating dry run only, while execute authorises attested mutation.
  • Aggregate budget. ExecutionBudget caps cumulative wall and CPU seconds, peak memory, and the number of executed steps. Every plan step's declared per-step budget must fit within the aggregate ceiling.
from rigor_foundry.remediation_authority import ExecutionAuthority, ExecutionBudget

budget = ExecutionBudget.build(
    wall_seconds=3600, cpu_seconds=3600, memory_mb=1024, max_steps=10
)
authority = ExecutionAuthority.build(
    approved_plan,
    budget,
    authority_id="authority-1",
    repository_id="repo-a",
    granted_by="release-owner",
    granted_at="2026-07-15T12:10:00Z",
    expires_at="2026-07-15T18:10:00Z",
    mode="execute",
)

authority.authorises(plan) is true only for the exact approved plan the grant binds.

docs.title: Attested execution ledger
docs.text:
ExecutionLedger.admit records an attested execution against a plan, an authority, and covering isolation claims. It proves the execution invariants and never performs the work:

  • Authority and order. The authority must bind the exact approved plan, the window must not run backwards, and the lane executions must follow the plan's dependency- and conflict-safe batches exactly.
  • Isolation. Each lane names one in-repository ExecutionClaim whose write set covers the lane's write set; claims are unique.
  • Step fidelity. Each StepOutcome matches its plan step, carries the plan step's idempotency key, fits the authority budget, and — when executed — captures evidence covering the step's declared outputs. A rolled-back step must correspond to a step that declared a rollback.
  • Budget, idempotency, mode. Cumulative consumption stays within the aggregate budget, an idempotency key never attests two divergent outcomes, and observe authority admits no executed step.
  • Failure propagation. A lane is skipped exactly when a prerequisite lane failed; a lane whose prerequisite failed may not have run.

The ledger resolves to succeeded, failed, or rolled-back and is content-addressed.

from rigor_foundry.remediation_executor import ExecutionLedger

ledger = ExecutionLedger.admit(
    plan=approved_plan,
    authority=authority,
    lane_executions=(base_execution, dependent_execution),
    claims=(base_claim, dependent_claim),
    started_at="2026-07-15T12:15:00Z",
    finished_at="2026-07-15T12:20:00Z",
)
print(ledger.resolution)

ExecutionLedger.from_dict re-verifies structural integrity, the resolution, and the self-contained mode, budget, and idempotency invariants; the plan-bound checks are the admission gate in admit. Both surfaces are reachable via submodule import (rigor_foundry.remediation_authority and rigor_foundry.remediation_executor).

docs.title: Content-addressed report differences
docs.text:
rigor report-diff compares two integrity-verified audit reports and emits one schema-1.0, content-addressed evidence record. It never scans a repository and never treats a missing historical report as an empty candidate set.

rigor report-diff \
  --before evidence/report-before.json \
  --after evidence/report-after.json \
  --output evidence/report-diff.json

Without --output, the deterministic JSON document is written to stdout. An explicit output is created exclusively and its parent must already exist.

docs.title: Transition classes
docs.text:
The record binds both exact report_digest values and partitions candidate identities into four classes:

  • retained_candidate_ids contains exact candidate identities present in both reports;
  • appeared_candidate_ids contains unmatched identities from the after report;
  • resolved_candidate_ids contains unmatched identities from the before report;
  • anchor_changes pairs candidates whose rule, path, symbol, evidence, confidence, rationale, and verification are identical while the exact anchor changed.

Changing evidence or any other semantic field is therefore one resolved plus one appeared candidate, not an anchor relocation. The operator chooses the before/after direction. The record does not prove Git ancestry or chronology.

docs.title: Ambiguous anchor changes
docs.text:
One unmatched semantic identity on each side is paired automatically. Multiple possible pairings fail closed. Resolve that ambiguity with a separate strict JSON document:

{
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "matches": [
    {
      "before_candidate_id": "<64 lowercase hex characters>",
      "after_candidate_id": "<64 lowercase hex characters>",
      "rationale": "Retained review evidence that establishes this relocation"
    }
  ]
}

Pass it with --anchor-matches PATH. Every declared candidate may be used once, both candidates must exist in the unmatched sets, and their semantic identities must agree. The pair and rationale become part of diff_digest.

docs.title: Compatibility declarations
docs.text:
Repository-root or Git-object-format, branch, policy, rule-pack, and scanner changes are incompatible by default. A deliberate comparison must name every actual change and include one non-empty justification:

rigor report-diff \
  --before evidence/old.json \
  --after evidence/new.json \
  --declare-policy-change \
  --declare-rule-pack-change \
  --justification "Reviewed migration from policy A to policy B"

Available flags are --declare-repository-change, --declare-branch-change, --declare-policy-change, --declare-rule-pack-change, and --declare-scanner-change. A missing declaration and a superfluous declaration both fail. This prevents a caller from silently comparing unlike evidence or pre-authorising differences that did not occur.

docs.title: Replay and interpretation boundary
docs.text:
ReportDiff.from_dict and ReportDiff.from_path require the exact before and after reports. They rebuild the compatibility checks, transition partition, automatic and declared anchor matches, and final digest. Rehashing a modified JSON object is insufficient when it no longer replays from those parents.

The diff is an evidence primitive for measured trends and reviewer effort. An appeared candidate is not automatically a regression, a resolved candidate is not automatically a fix, and a retained candidate is not automatically valid. Correctness still requires exact-report review evidence.

docs.title: Repository file input observations
docs.text:
The provisional module API observe_repository_file_inputs combines actual Git inputs with complete baseline blob reads and current file observations within that Git path domain. The caller supplies an exact, already authorised worktree root, full baseline commit, actual GitRunner and explicit PolicyReadBudget1.

RepositoryFileInputs retains its bounding RepositoryGitInputs, plus sorted baseline_files and current_files arrays of RepositoryFileRow. Current paths are the complete union of baseline paths, every index stage and nonignored untracked paths. Deleted or renamed baseline paths remain present; staged blob IDs remain distinct from actual current file-byte identities.

Baseline blobs are read by their full object IDs. The API computes both their SHA-256 and Git blob identity from those actual bytes, refusing content that does not match the requested Git object. Baseline gitlinks retain commit identities without being coerced into file bytes. Regular current files use the existing descriptor-relative stable reader, with explicit byte bounds and no-follow parent traversal. Symlinks retain their link bytes without following targets. Missing paths are explicit deleted rows. Directories, including submodule worktrees, and other unsupported leaf types remain unsupported rows; their separate maintained-root owner is still required.

All rows keep null language and role until an independent owner classifies them. No unknown row is discarded or declared outside maintained scope.

The transaction counts the actual standard-output/error bytes of its first Git observation, then both complete file observations, and supplies only the remaining byte budget to the closing Git observation. Each Git observation includes its own two matching reads. Baseline/current file observations must agree, bounding Git state must agree, and the root pathname must still name the retained directory object. Unique path count, path depth, individual file bytes and aggregate bytes are bounded. Refusal returns no partial inventory or alternate root.

The returned source_bytes_read counts the complete actual transaction, including the closing Git observation. It is auxiliary accounting and does not change semantic equality. An enclosing collector may supply maximum_paths to tighten the original source/reference ceiling, including zero for an actual empty Git tree. See Configured inventory inputs for combined Git/directory capture accounting and shared classification.

These are source observations, not an atomic Git/filesystem snapshot or an authenticated maintained inventory. Configured ignored/generated/disjoint roots, complete classification, task/fact contexts and admission remain the enclosing installed owner's responsibilities. Existing source-access and snapshot/lifetime permission must already be held. Git provenance is not a network sandbox. Retained-directory Git execution requires Linux /proc/self/fd; no Windows or other native-host qualification is implied.

docs.title: Repository Git input observations
docs.text:
The provisional observe_repository_git_inputs Python API reads an explicitly selected Git worktree with a full baseline commit ID, an actual GitRunner and an explicit PolicyReadBudget1. It retains a no-follow directory descriptor during the read. Git runs from that retained directory, rather than discovering a containing repository from an arbitrary caller path. A subdirectory or symlink root refuses.

The returned RepositoryGitInputs keeps the baseline commit and tree, current HEAD and tree, SHA-1 or SHA-256 object format, complete recursive baseline modes and object IDs, every current index stage, nonignored untracked paths, original NUL-delimited status output and executable provenance. Unresolved index stages remain visible. They are not coerced into a stage-zero inventory. Deleted or renamed baseline paths remain in the baseline entries.

Each command enforces a streaming output ceiling. The transaction also counts all command outputs against its total byte budget. Two complete observations must agree, and the canonical root must still name the retained directory object. These checks detect disagreement; they do not establish an atomic filesystem snapshot.

source_bytes_read counts actual standard-output/error bytes across both complete Git reads. It supports enclosing transaction accounting and is excluded from semantic observation equality. This resource counter supplies no source-authentication or snapshot authority.

This API observes Git inputs only. It does not read or classify every current file, enrol ignored/generated roots, authenticate a task, grant source access, prove maintained-inventory completeness, or authorise an effect. Those remain the enclosing installed owner's responsibilities. The caller must already hold source-access permission and the applicable snapshot/lifetime guards. No missing input triggers an alternate repository or scan fallback.

The retained-directory execution path currently requires Linux /proc/self/fd. No Windows qualification is implied by parsing a portable Git object identity.

parse_git_baseline_entries and parse_git_untracked_paths expose the same bounded format contracts for retained original Git output. They parse bytes without invoking Git or accessing a repository; malformed, incomplete, duplicate or over-budget entries refuse.

docs.title: Rule-chain candidate inspection
docs.text:
rigor_foundry.rule_chain_candidate.inspect_rule_chain_candidate is a read-only Python API for checking whether one proposed semantic transition, its signed review, retained StandardPack sources, and a signed ProjectProfile refer to the same exact objects. It composes the host-selected discovery and native-source readers, review verifier, pack verifiers, and profile selection. It does not fetch a remote source or assign a numeric freshness lifetime.

The caller supplies the exact proposal artefact and source captures, typed v2 pack and profile objects, a host-composed semantic-review verifier, one host-composed retained-source verifier per selected pack, the role-separated trust policies, the expected project and scope, and an explicit UTC instant. The host must protect selections and revocations throughout its leases. A caller-controlled test provider can exercise the API but cannot enrol live authority. A signed clear review is checked as a source dependency; the reviewer must have a separate identity and trusted signing key from the author. Role construction now explicitly supplies semantic_authors and semantic_reviewers alongside the three existing rule-chain policies. Semantic key records carry caller-selected, digest-bound v2 identities; the three other roles retain v1 records. All role key material is distinct, and semantic author and reviewer identity sets are disjoint ignoring case. The host still authenticates the selected review identities and exact expected objects. The review verifier additionally binds the named reviewer to its exact enrolled key identity and requires the named author to belong to the selected author policy, using case-insensitive enrollment comparisons. The role policies' disjointness then prevents a named author from holding a reviewer key.

The result is RuleChainCandidateReport. Its digest binds the proposal, review acceptance dependency, profile, packs, selected authority clauses and reviewer policy. guard_admissible is always False. A report is neither a signed EffectiveProfileLock nor an active dispatch permit. It cannot resolve local constraints, current grants, adapter custody, revocation or mutable evidence state, and it cannot authorise an effect. The v1 pack, profile, audit-lock and dispatch formats remain unchanged; no automatic CLI or Guard cutover occurs.

Applications that need an active gate must separately implement and select a reviewed effective lock, verify current state and grant authority before each effect, and obtain rollout authority. Reusing this inspection result as an effect permission is a contract violation.

docs.title: Signed acceptance and selected v2 locks
docs.text:
semantic_transition_acceptance_v2.SignedSemanticAcceptanceV2 binds a complete accepted-semantic-transition.v2 body to an external reviewer Ed25519 signature in domain rigor-foundry.semantic-transition-acceptance.v2. The body records exactly four successor links, statement hashes, discovery selection and byte budgets, author attribution, source and native ratification hashes, reviewer identity and declared review time. Envelope parsing recomputes digests; verify_signature() checks the real signature, current key lifecycle, attribution relation and distinct author/reviewer identities.

ReviewerIdentityPolicy binds every selected key to exactly one reviewer. Identity uniqueness and enrollment agreement both ignore case. A v2 enrolled key cannot be relabelled; legacy v1 keys retain explicit mappings in this data API, while the five-role v2 chain requires identity-bearing semantic policies. ProposalAuthorAttribution records selected attestation evidence and a canonical session UUID; its digest does not authenticate the attesting host.

HostSemanticAcceptanceVerifierV2.verify() reads the selected policy, revocations, review and native source under a host lease. It checks the discovery digest on the same held semantic-source state that the existing source verifier consumes. It also compares the retained findings bytes and the exact four source spans. The returned dependency has guard_admissible == False. Native human-origin markers and capture integrity remain subject to the source-custody limits in canonical clause semantics.

rule_chain_candidate_v2.inspect_rule_chain_candidate_v2() joins that acceptance with the signed packs and profile, requiring four exact selected successors and the current five role policies. RuleChainCandidateReportV2 is a read-only report; it does not select a lock.

rule_chain_lock_v2.EffectiveProfileLockV2 carries a complete signed projection: selected clauses and freshness policies, constraints, exclusions, adapter custody, issuer order, acceptance selection, effect-operation catalogue and resolver-code pins. Its body() and build() APIs validate and bind the complete projection. Parsing and signature attachment establish integrity; verify_structural_lock() additionally checks the current signed chain, retained sources, adapter records, selected preconditions and active resolver signature. Held locks retain blocking contradictions and refuse effective verification. The body() signature remains on the public class; its implementation is inherited from an internal projection owner.

selected_rule_chain_host_v2.HostSelectedRuleChainVerifierV2 freshly rebuilds the acceptance and candidate before trusting a selected lock. verified_lease() repeats those checks after the consumer and refuses a changed closing proof. The host provider pins state and revocations for the entire context and authenticates their custody. A caller-created provider demonstrates behavior without establishing operational trust.

docs.title: Closed first-operation dependencies
docs.text:
ExtractorRegistryV2 and AdapterOperationsV2 accept only their empty bootstrap bodies or the fixed atomic-replacement candidate. The three declared extractor entrypoints are present in rigor_foundry.tier0_builtin: extract_content_byte_count.extract, extract_fixed_variant.extract and extract_path_target.extract. Registry module names are metadata, not a dynamic loader or proof of installed code identity.

AtomicFileReplaceInvocationV2.from_bytes() parses a closed canonical wire for local-file-write.atomic-replace: requested path, standard canonical base64 content, and separate declared target, count and variant. Decoded replacement content is at most 16 MiB; each path is at most 4095 UTF-8 bytes. extract_atomic_file_replace_v2() compares all declarations with the actual content length, fixed replace-or-create variant and host-canonicalized path. A supplied callback is an observation interface, not an admission capability.

derive_selected_path_scope_v2() derives current project/group roots from exact selected registry bytes, including inactive registrations; the selected project must be active. It accepts explicit profiled roots and performs no filesystem lookup. Historical aliases do not become current registered roots. extract_atomic_file_replace_for_scope_v2() uses that selected scope through real descriptor-backed no-follow path admission. Linux x86-64 openat2 refuses symlinks, traversal, mount crossings during target descent, repository internals and nested or unregistered repositories. Missing final leaves may be created; their parent must exist. All observations and descriptors close before the extraction call returns, and every failure becomes a chained PermissionError. The direct callback API propagates callback errors.

These APIs extract and verify read-only dependencies. They install no handler, write no replacement file, grant no permit and change no stable CLI or v1 serialized contract. Actual execution still requires protected installed-code custody, current action applicability, grants, permits and final revalidation.

Selected dispatch applicability composes the actual selected extractor with active admits, vetoes and constraints under the same retained chain and semantics context. Journal-backed rate constraints read the real retained history and its original catalogues. These evaluated results remain read-only data with guard_admissible == False.

docs.title: SARIF export
docs.text:
RigorFoundry emits deterministic SARIF 2.1.0 Errata 01 without converting static audit candidates into defect verdicts.

rigor sarif --report report.json --output results.sarif
rigor sarif --report report.json --review reviews.json --output results.sarif

The command verifies report integrity and validates every supplied review. Duplicate, incomplete, foreign, or stale review records fail closed. Omitting --output writes the same deterministic JSON to stdout.

docs.title: State mapping
docs.text:
RigorFoundry state SARIF kind SARIF level unreviewed candidate review note needs-evidence review note reviewed valid, P0/P1 fail error reviewed valid, P2 fail warning reviewed valid, P3/P4 fail note reviewed invalid notApplicable none reviewed accepted-boundary informational note

Every report candidate remains a result. The property bag records separate rigorFoundry/candidateState and rigorFoundry/verdictState values, so a SARIF consumer can distinguish scanner evidence from a human evidence decision. Severity provenance is review-record only when a validated review provides a severity.

docs.title: Identity and anchors
docs.text:
Rule IDs and indices come from the complete versioned RigorFoundry rule pack. The content-addressed candidate ID is exported as the exact rigorFoundry/v1 fingerprint. RigorFoundry does not claim a GitHub primaryLocationLineHash without the scanned line bytes required to compute that separate identity. Locations use percent-encoded repository-relative paths and inclusive spans.

The rigorFoundry/anchor property preserves the strict anchor schema. A tracked-blob result includes the exact scanned Git blob OID and content SHA-256. A repository-tree result includes the exact HEAD tree OID and complete tracked-content SHA-256. Run properties also bind the report, policy, ignored inventory, tracked content, rule-pack, HEAD, tree, and Git object format.

The schema URI is exported as SARIF_SCHEMA_URI; its current value identifies the OASIS SARIF 2.1.0 Errata 01 JSON schema. report_sarif and the schema/version constants are provisional package-level APIs. Their lifecycle is independent of the stable SARIF wire contract; see Public API stability.

docs.title: Scientific and numerical correctness rules
docs.text: Rule-pack rigor-foundry/1.13.0 adds the bounded scientific category (prefix SN). Findings are anchored needs-evidence candidates, not proof that a numerical result is wrong or a stochastic test is flaky.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rule Signal Confidence SN001-exact-float-equality-in-test a Python test function compares a direct signed or unsigned float literal with == or != high SN002-unseeded-stochastic-test an explicitly imported supported random or numpy.random API is used before local deterministic seeding, or a supported generator is constructed without a seed high

SN001 is deliberately narrower than type inference. It ignores integer, Decimal, container, and string comparisons, and explicit approx or isclose operands. Reviewers should replace accidental exactness with a justified absolute/relative tolerance, while preserving exact comparison when the test really specifies binary identity, parsing, or serialisation.

SN002 resolves explicit module and direct imports for a bounded set of common draw APIs. It treats random.seed, numpy.random.seed, random.Random, and numpy.random.default_rng as deterministic only when a non-None seed is supplied before the relevant draw. Module-level seeds, custom wrappers, fixtures, and arbitrary generator data flow are not inferred. Reviewers should seed locally before the first draw or prove that an external fixture establishes the exact replay contract.

Only tracked UTF-8 .py files classified as tests by repository policy or test naming are parsed. Invalid Python yields no SN candidate because the existing unparseable-test authenticity rule owns that condition. Evidence contains exact tracked-blob and line/file digests without copying source text.

The family contributes a portable control to the scientific-numerical-correctness audit domain. Both rules enter maturity probation; enforcement still requires adjudicated cross-repository precision, false-positive, and reviewer-effort evidence.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Treat repository names, paths, file content, configuration, native-tool output, and archive members as adversarial input.

  • Inventory resolves Git only from fixed or operator-declared trust roots, rejects symlinked roots/components, enforces a half-open version interval, hashes the executable, pins the validated descriptor where the platform exposes descriptor execution, and detects replacement before and after every command. Platforms without a descriptor execution path fail closed. Multi-link executables are rejected; POSIX mode checks also reject group/world-writable and elevated-ID executables at validation and hashing. Snapshot and execution opens walk every absolute component through no-follow directory descriptors, so a post-validation intermediate symlink cannot become the trusted baseline.
  • Git plumbing receives a minimal environment without ambient configuration, credentials, prompts, replacement objects, or optional index locks. The runner disables repository-local filesystem monitors and redirects hooks to a reserved absent path under the trust root. The declared trust root must itself be protected from untrusted writers; an occupied reserved hook path fails closed.
  • Native processes require explicit consent and use fixed-root executable resolution, argv-only invocation, a credential-free environment, a no-network read-only bubblewrap sandbox, mandatory timeouts, process-tree termination, disabled nested user namespaces, and a streaming aggregate output hard cap. Bubblewrap must satisfy a versioned compatibility policy; evidence records its semantic version, executable digest, dpkg-reported package association/version/architecture/status, package-query executable digest, required-option surface, and policy identity, then verifies the same identity after execution.
  • Gate and campaign artifacts retain native execution digests, bounded counts, and structured secret-free sandbox provenance; raw argv, environment values, source excerpts, command output, and package-manager output are excluded. The dpkg association is package-database evidence, not proof of a repository signature or installed-payload checksum; the executable digest identifies the inspected and executed binary bytes.
  • Built-in profiles copy only exact clean tracked regular files into a bounded read-only snapshot, mount the analyser from a retained descriptor, and bind executable, configuration, input, version-output, output, and profile digests. Ignored/untracked files, symlinks, gitlinks, hard links, concurrent replacement, malformed output, timeouts, truncation, and analyser errors cannot become clean evidence. The offline Trivy profile claims only misconfiguration and secret scanning, never CVE or supply-chain coverage. The offline OSV profile requires an exact tracked database manifest, verifies every externally supplied official-layout archive without following links, and mounts only the verified snapshot into the no-network sandbox. Missing, mutated, linked, malformed, unsafe, or oversized database content is unavailable evidence, never a clean result. OSV matches do not establish reachability, exploitability, remediation priority, or an adjudicated verdict.
  • Repository policies must be tracked, non-symlink UTF-8 files inside the audited root, and Git index modes and object ids bind every tracked entry.
  • Bootstrap writes walk existing parents through retained no-follow directory descriptors, create single-link regular files with exclusive creation, synchronize file and parent metadata, and revalidate root, parent, path, and Git tracked/ignored state before returning. A review ledger present at either validation sample is rejected; absence is not an atomic reservation, so a concurrent creator can populate the declared path after the final sample. A failed two-file attempt preserves any file it created as incident evidence: pathname-based rollback is intentionally forbidden because POSIX cannot atomically prove an inode identity and unlink that same inode. Concurrently replaced data is never deleted by bootstrap.
  • Writes require an explicit command and a validated ignored destination. Campaign persistence and TODO promotion require the ignored-path check to reproduce the executable provenance already bound to the durable evidence.
  • Missing evidence never becomes pass.
  • External source capture records declared HTTPS acquisition metadata and exact retained bytes; it is not publisher-signature or source-authority proof. Verification runs offline, is scoped to the explicit retrieval policy, and grants no remediation, waiver, suppression, or promotion authority.
  • SARIF export validates every supplied review against the exact report and retains unreviewed or needs-evidence candidates as review results. Only a completed valid review supplies defect severity. Repository-relative paths are URI-encoded while exact anchor paths and object identities remain in the RigorFoundry property bag.
  • Pack and reviewer clearance requires real Ed25519 verification against an explicit integrity-bound public-key trust store. The signed message includes a versioned length-prefixed protocol domain, so standard-pack signatures cannot replay as reviewer attestations even when a key is shared. Legacy raw-digest signatures and domainless envelopes fail closed. Key identifiers and raw public keys must both be unique, so aliases for one underlying key cannot satisfy independent-review quorum; labels and digest-shaped strings do not establish trust.
  • CI actions, Python dependencies, the base image, downloaded executables, CodeQL bundle, BuildKit image, and local Docker-action images are immutably pinned. Project-controlled release downloads verify the retained manifest and final executable or archive before use.
  • GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 and official setup-python provisioning retain a bounded provider-managed manifest residual. Runner labels, action commits, and Python patch releases are exact; cache identity is repository- and lockfile-scoped. Issue 9 tracks the remaining per-artifact identity gap.
  • The consumer Action pins its nested action and hash-locks build/runtime installation. Inputs cross the shell boundary only through quoted environment values. Output targets must be absent, and in-repository targets must be untracked and ignored. The system pre-commit hook requires a separately hash-locked RigorFoundry installation. Both defaults are observe-only and carry no promotion or remediation command.
  • Package publication uses a protected OIDC environment rather than a stored package credential.

docs.title: Dependency advisory audits
docs.text:
The Security workflow audits all seven hash-locked Python profiles (build, CI, fuzz, native, runtime, security and test) and the VS Code extension's committed npm lock on every push and pull request to main. Python audits require hashes, avoid installation and fail when dependency collection fails. The npm audit includes development dependencies and uses the default failure threshold. Advisory findings and registry errors block the jobs.

The repository's dependency-waiver guard also checks the actual Git-visible lock inventory, exact scanner commands, event enrolment and the aggregate security-gate. Both scanner jobs must succeed, including when one is skipped or cancelled. Adding another lock requires explicit audit enrolment; an unsupported lock fails the guard. The current waiver set must remain empty; the guard rejects a nonempty set and any --ignore-vuln workflow option. These source checks do not prove that hosted branch protection requires the gate or that the current head has passed a hosted audit.

docs.title: GitHub-hosted AppArmor boundary
docs.text:
Ubuntu 24.04 mediates unprivileged user namespaces and requires applications that need them to be explicitly allowed by an AppArmor profile. The CI runner therefore retains a path-specific /usr/bin/bwrap profile with flags=(unconfined) and one userns, rule. This profile is deliberately not claimed as the native-audit sandbox: it is only the compatibility attachment that lets the root-owned Bubblewrap executable create the initial namespace. The audited Bubblewrap argument contract supplies the read-only, no-network, credential-free boundary and disables nested user namespaces. See Ubuntu's unprivileged user namespace restriction and Bubblewrap's sandbox security contract.

CI remains pinned to the Ubuntu 24.04 runner family, asserts that the global restriction is still enabled, loads only the path-specific profile, records the installed package/version, and executes the same compatibility flags in a smoke sandbox. Regression tests reject a global sysctl disable, additional AppArmor permissions, profile removal, or omission of nested-userns disabling. A compromised runner administrator, kernel, root-owned package database, or root-owned launcher is outside this boundary; RigorFoundry detects identity or package drift during an audit but does not claim to withstand a compromised host root.

Do not disclose a suspected vulnerability in a public issue. Follow the security policy and use private vulnerability reporting.

docs.title: Security-tool lock maintenance
docs.text:
The current security lock pins Semgrep 1.180.0 and Click 8.4.2. Its retained generation header names pip-compile on Python 3.11, matching the repository lock target. Use a Python 3.11 environment with the pip-tools version pinned in requirements/ci.txt and retain the complete CI constraints and SHA-256 hashes. Regenerate from the repository root:

python3.11 -m piptools compile --allow-unsafe --generate-hashes --strip-extras \
  --upgrade --constraint requirements/ci.txt \
  --output-file requirements/security.txt requirements/security.in

Keep the canonical seven-line licence header above the generated header. After regeneration, run the strict audit and install the entire hash-locked profile in a fresh environment; run pip check, Bandit and the installed semgrep console entry point with the repository policy. The local lock qualification does not establish hosted CI or runtime admission.

docs.title: Selected dispatch applicability
docs.text:
evaluate_selected_dispatch_applicability_v2() composes actual request extraction and clause evaluation under one selected source context. The application supplies its authenticated semantics verifier, installed constraint reader, and the lock and projection digests observed by that task's boot. The request cannot choose these sources.

from rigor_foundry.selected_dispatch_applicability_v2 import (
    evaluate_selected_dispatch_applicability_v2,
)

# These values come from the application's installed providers and current boot.
evaluated = evaluate_selected_dispatch_applicability_v2(
    request,
    verifier=installed_semantics_verifier,
    observed_lock_digest=task_lock_digest,
    observed_projection_digest=task_projection_digest,
    context_for=installed_constraint_reader,
)
assert evaluated.guard_admissible is False

The function enters HostSelectedClauseSemanticsVerifierV2.verified_context() once. That context yields the selected semantics, the actual held chain state, and its verified proof. Extraction and evaluation use that same chain, without reopening the chain provider. The function returns only after closing source checks succeed. The older two-value verified_lease() API retains its existing shape and closing checks.

docs.title: Actual extraction and applicability
docs.text:
The selected extractor checks the complete canonical invocation against the selected adapter, operation catalogue, extractor registry, path scope, lock and projection. The first operation is local-file-write.atomic-replace. Its decoded content, target and fixed variant must match the declarations. Its descriptor-backed path check closes before extraction returns.

Every ordered part then requires an active covering admit. A covering veto refuses. All applicable constraints must pass the fixed evaluator boundary. Concrete selector containment respects path component boundaries and exclusions. The first operation has no registered route extractor: an applicable route constraint refuses before reading an installed route context.

The four public built-in evaluators use the canonical semantics parameter rules, including closed fields, valid UTC ranges and finite decimal ceilings. The window evaluator validates every range before testing applicability; a matching early range cannot hide a malformed later range. Precondition context is host-computed evidence. The selected authority requirement determines which effect classes require enforced custody; a cooperative check cannot satisfy that requirement for those classes.

SelectedDispatchApplicabilityV2 retains actual extraction, the semantics proof and the ordered StageBResultV2 results. Direct record construction does not reproduce verification. No new stable CLI command or wire version is introduced by this module-level Python API.

docs.title: Journal-backed rate context
docs.text:
An installed EffectJournalRateSourceV2 binds the actual extracted part before reading its rate clauses. The application holds a real EffectJournalStoreV2 exclusive lease for those reads and independently supplies the complete-history origin, fresh UTC clock, verified honoured closures and each historical operation's original catalogue.

The source rescans the retained descriptor for every rate read. It checks full frame consistency and operation replay, including records appended beyond an earlier selected prefix. Missing history or catalogue, changed bytes, overlapping open targets and unusable clock data refuse. An operation intent still counts after its independently honoured closure. The signed window includes its start boundary. A new journal header cannot prove that the whole window was retained.

Journal reads and append durability use shared internal descriptor I/O. They do not import the permit-consumption ledger or select grant accounting. This operation replay contract refuses event kinds whose semantics it does not implement, including partial-operation, target-reconciliation, trust-activation and key-revocation events. A frame accepted by the journal parser does not make such history usable by this consumer; it cannot silently ignore those events.

docs.title: Execution boundary
docs.text:
Applicability leaves the target file unchanged and supplies no grant, reserved use, effect permit or handler capability. guard_admissible is always false. The application still needs protected installed-code and source custody, current grants and permits, transaction accounting, final revalidation and a qualified handler before performing an effect. Fixture signatures and native format transcripts demonstrate test integrity; they establish no owner ratification or protected deployment.

See canonical clause semantics and rule-chain candidate inspection for the underlying source and native-capture boundaries.

docs.title: Verified external source provenance
docs.text:
RigorFoundry schema 1.0 records and verifies exact externally cited advisories, versions, standards, and content digests. It is deliberately split into four content-addressed records:

  1. ExternalSourceClaim states the exact subject, predicate, expected value, HTTPS source, and extraction procedure.
  2. SourceRetrievalPolicy declares allowed hosts, redirect boundaries, timeout, byte limit, media types, and freshness.
  3. SourceCapture binds retained raw response bytes to acquisition metadata, the retrieval policy, and the declared retriever identity.
  4. SourceVerification exists only after deterministic offline verification succeeds against those exact retained bytes.

Changing a claim changes its verification. Changing retrieval policy changes the capture and therefore its verification. These relationships are registered in the digest dependency graph.

docs.title: Epistemic boundary
docs.text:
A canonical HTTPS URI and response digest prove which bytes were reviewed. They do not prove publisher authorship, uncompromised DNS or TLS, or universal truth. SourceVerification.authority_scope is consequently fixed to retrieval-policy-only. A genuine publisher signature requires a separate signature-verification record; TLS capture must never be represented as one.

The capture command performs no network access. It records response bytes already retained by an explicitly authorised retriever. Network authority, proxy policy, private-address rejection, credentials, decompression, and redirect execution therefore remain outside deterministic offline verification. The record preserves declared retriever name, semantic version, and executable SHA-256 without inventing executable attestation.

No claim or verification grants permission to modify a repository, accept a risk, suppress a vulnerability, or promote an audit candidate.

docs.title: Claim methods
docs.text:
advisory, version, and standard claims require json-pointer extraction. The selector must be a non-empty RFC 6901 pointer resolving to one exact JSON scalar. Parsing is UTF-8 only, rejects non-finite numbers and duplicate object keys, and preserves scalar types: JSON true cannot satisfy numeric 1.

content-digest claims require predicate sha256, method whole-payload-sha256, an empty selector, and one lowercase SHA-256 value. They verify raw retained bytes without parsing or redistributing licensed or paywalled content.

docs.title: Retained-payload workflow
docs.text:
Record one retained response:

rigor source-capture \
  --policy source-policy.json \
  --payload advisory-response.json \
  --requested-uri https://advisories.example.test/CVE-2026-52869.json \
  --final-uri https://advisories.example.test/CVE-2026-52869.json \
  --redirect-count 0 \
  --http-status 200 \
  --media-type application/json \
  --retrieved-at 2026-07-17T08:00:00Z \
  --retriever-name curl \
  --retriever-version 8.10.1 \
  --retriever-executable-digest 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef \
  --output source-capture.json

Verify offline against the same payload:

rigor source-verify \
  --claim source-claim.json \
  --capture source-capture.json \
  --payload advisory-response.json \
  --verified-at 2026-07-17T08:30:00Z \
  --verifier auditor/one \
  --output source-verification.json

The payload reader performs component-wise no-follow traversal, requires a single-link regular file, derives size and SHA-256 from one stable descriptor pass, enforces the policy byte limit, and fails closed if the file changes. Output parents must already exist.

docs.title: Public Python API
docs.text:
These top-level imports are provisional:

from rigor_foundry import (
    ExternalSourceClaim,
    SourceCapture,
    SourceRetrievalPolicy,
    SourceVerification,
    read_source_payload,
    source_provenance_to_json,
    verify_external_source,
)

Use build, record, from_dict, or verify_external_source; direct success-shaped dataclass construction is unavailable. Parsers require exact fields, recompute derived digests, reject unsupported schema versions, and reject source URI, verified-value, type, or freshness contradictions across a verification record. SourceVerification.from_dict cannot replay extraction because records omit retained payload bytes. At an evidence trust boundary, retain the payload and call verify_external_source again; an internally consistent parsed record alone is not extraction proof.

docs.title: Retained source universe
docs.text: The provisional Python source APIs preserve the complete host-selected policy source cohort and verify its actual original bytes. They keep unused, unread, unavailable, protected and excluded sources explicit. Byte integrity and a complete partition are prerequisites for a later corpus consumer; they do not establish semantic completeness, accepted exclusions, ready boot or effects.

docs.title: Original source formats
docs.text:
policy_source_records.PolicySourceRecord1 adapts the actual original models to the retained context-source interface. It preserves every original field, version and owning digest. parse_policy_source_record(kind, value, budget=budget) selects a fixed parser with explicit collection/depth bounds. Request data cannot appoint a loader, parser or source location.

Source kind Exact original format Original identity and digest source-capture 1.0 Complete SourceCapture.capture_digest for both fields native-source-pin native-source-pin.v1 Original source_id and pin_digest discovery-source-receipt discovery-source-closure.v1 Original receipt_digest for both fields

The capture reference identifies the complete acquisition record, rather than the payload hash alone. The native pin retains the original full JSONL-file and exact question/reply selectors. Parsing either remains a metadata check.

discovery_source_receipt.DiscoverySourceReceipt1 parses the existing output of validate_discovery_sources. It adds no object_kind to that original receipt and defines no replacement digest. Original sorted source/shard rows, unused source IDs, manifest hash, candidate/span counts and DiscoveryLimits remain intact. Its original status is discovery-integrity-verified, assertion class is declared-snapshot-integrity-only and promotable remains false. Explicit policy parser budgets do not rewrite those embedded original limits.

docs.title: Actual source selection and lifetime
docs.text:
retained_policy_source.RetainedPolicySource holds an independently selected raw file and its parent directory through use and closing checks. The host already owns access; opaque universe locators never become file paths.

from rigor_foundry.retained_policy_source import RetainedPolicySource

with RetainedPolicySource(
    original_path,
    byte_digest=selected_byte_sha256,
    byte_count=selected_byte_count,
    budget=budget,
) as retained_bytes:
    original_payload = retained_bytes.read()

Every read checks complete exact bytes, the single-link regular-file policy, no-follow traversal, retained file/parent identities and individual byte limits. Empty files remain actual zero-byte sources. Changes or replacement invalidate the held selection. Closure repeats the check and releases both owned descriptors even when it refuses; later use fails. A new lease of equal bytes has a different selection identity. No fetch or duplicate prose tree is created by these APIs.

policy_source_selection.PolicySourceSelection borrows the original metadata lease and optional raw lease. Its source ID, classification, opaque locator, read state, disposition and optional decision ID are explicit host choices. Held rows have no installed raw, native or discovery reader. Their metadata can remain present even when the original payload is unavailable.

Verified HTTPS captures compare actual raw count/hash with the original capture. Verified native selections use the actual HostNativeSourceVerifier and current host pin/revocations, original captures, full file hash and exact original file path. A caller-supplied native pin is not a trusted host state. The original native verification remains integrity evidence, not issuer or semantic authority.

Verified discovery selections additionally borrow DiscoverySourceSelection: an explicit original root, manifest name and original DiscoveryLimits. They join the retained raw path/count/hash to the actual manifest and rerun the unchanged complete original validator. Original processing limits must fit the current explicit policy budget. Neither a receipt alone nor a local Markdown file relabelled as an HTTPS capture proves that observation.

docs.title: Complete fixed owner
docs.text:
source_universe_owner.SourceUniverseOwner requires the entire immutable, source-ID-sorted cohort, actual retained registry/producer-contract files and a prior complete package/interpreter observation. Its fixed implementation ID is builtin.policy-source-universe.v1, owner class source; its independent subject kinds are source-bytes and source-record, with no fact namespace. The contract must enroll the actual registry and original source formats. Root project/group/path relations are checked against the original registry. Those descriptive bindings do not grant access to external source material.

from rigor_foundry.source_universe_owner import SourceUniverseOwner

# All inputs are actual host selections, already held by their owning contexts.
with SourceUniverseOwner(
    sources=selected_sources,
    registry_source=selected_registry,
    contract_source=selected_source_contract,
    implementation=observed_code,
    budget=budget,
) as owner:
    universe = owner.observe()
    owner.verify(universe)
    checked_regions = owner.verify_partitions(
        universe, regions=declared_regions, spans=declared_statement_spans
    )

Every original discovery receipt contributes all its source rows, including unused empty sources. Missing rows refuse. A mixture of held and verified members refuses before calling any original discovery reader: complete snapshot validation must not ingest a protected member merely to qualify another row. An entirely held cohort remains representable without reading its original payload files.

The owner observes its complete actual package/interpreter, original sources, contract and registry before and after producing entries or consuming byte partitions. Selection snapshots bind the whole cohort and source verification results. Independent byte/record subjects precede enclosing entry/proof hashes; there is no self-referential context digest. verify recomputes the complete actual cohort, so a subset or a self-digested foreign declaration fails. Owner closure revalidates the borrowed selections; their host closes the underlying leases afterward. Repeated observations do not prove atomic or continuous multi-root custody between checks.

docs.title: Source entries and byte accounting
docs.text:
source_universe.SourceUniverseEntry1 has closed schema 1.0 fields: schema_version, object_kind, source_id, existing_source, classification, locator, byte_digest, byte_count, read_state, disposition, disposition_decision, provenance and entry_digest.

Classifications are public, internal, confidential and secret. Read states are verified, unread, unavailable and protected; dispositions are included and excluded. Verified rows require an exact byte hash/count. The fixed owner emits null byte metadata for held rows and binds their original record as the independent proof subject. An excluded row requires its exact decision ID and remains present. A decision ID alone does not prove that the competent semantic owner accepted that exclusion.

verify_partitions checks existing SourceRegion1 and optional SourceSpan1 records over the same actual held bytes for every included verified source. Regions retain source/byte order and partition the complete payload without gaps, overlap or omitted tails. Empty sources need no region. Rule, decision, span, source and combined byte budgets remain enforced. Foreign, held or excluded sources cannot supply partition bytes. Optional spans verify original byte bounds and hashes without changing statement offsets or newlines.

Parsing an entry or verifying its partition does not accept extraction meaning, grant source access, authenticate an initiating instruction/claim or qualify a selected policy/common gate. Relevant held sources and unresolved regions still require the enclosing corpus/host decision. These APIs emit no ready or admitted status.

verify_external_native_source(pin) checks that a separately verified original native approval carrier is outside the complete original corpus inputs. It rechecks the actual cohort, refuses a shared retained path or declared original payload digest, and includes held native metadata without opening protected bytes. This method does not authenticate the supplied pin. The enclosing corpus verifier first checks it through the actual native owner, then applies this source-independence check.

docs.title: 1.0 stable compatibility contract
docs.text:
RigorFoundry carries one digest-bound compatibility manifest targeting 1.0.0, the version declared by the current source metadata. Retrieve it from an installed wheel without consulting the source tree:

rigor contract

or from Python:

from rigor_foundry import stable_contract_manifest

manifest = stable_contract_manifest()

Source version, compatibility target and publication state are separate. The manifest defines the frozen contract in this source tree. Publication requires the release gates and explicit owner authorisation; verify an installable version in the public registry. Its SHA-256 contract_digest covers every field except the digest itself.

docs.title: What is frozen
docs.text:
The contract binds three different surfaces instead of treating package import success as universal compatibility:

  1. Stable Python imports. Eleven package-level names have exact runtime object, kind, module, and qualified-name checks. Other exported Python names remain explicitly provisional even when their serialized records are stable.
  2. CLI spellings. Every currently installed command, option spelling, and positional name is in the stable CLI set. CI rejects a removed, renamed, added-but-unclassified, or silently changed parser surface.
  3. Serialized protocols. The manifest names exact schema identifiers and versions, including reports, reviews, policies, anchors, campaigns, packs, maturity, enforcement, offline verification, CRA evidence, SARIF, OSCAL, remediation, provenance, work records, and adapter evidence. An AST guard requires every production *_SCHEMA_VERSION declaration to have an explicit classification: frozen, version-pinned provisional, or individually justified outside the frozen interchange. A serializer/parser using a bare string schema_version cannot evade the named inventory. Host-held proofs, private coordination formats, aliases and provisional candidate records outside the frozen set are named with their reasons in the test contract.

The manifest is authoritative for the exact command and schema inventory. The human documentation for each command or schema continues to define semantic preconditions, field meanings, authority boundaries, and failure modes.

The identity-bearing semantic key-policy wire at version 2.0 is explicitly provisional and separately version-pinned. The frozen verification-key-policy wire remains 1.0 with its original fields. Supplying an enrolled semantic identity selects the new record and changes its digest; this does not change the frozen manifest or enroll a live key. See public API stability for the consuming role boundary.

The inventory-domain, inventory-baseline, maintained-surface, maintained-inventory, fact-observation, fact-context, task-context and remediation-task-binding declarations are explicitly provisional at 1.0 and individually version-pinned. They do not extend the frozen manifest. Their source verification and authority boundaries remain defined in maintained contexts and task contexts.

The source-universe-entry declaration is also explicitly provisional at 1.0, individually version-pinned outside the frozen manifest. Its actual source owner reuses existing original HTTPS capture, native pin and discovery receipt formats without changing their versions, fields or owning digests.

The explicit rule declarations and qualitative contracts are also individually version-pinned provisional schemas. RuleScope1, SemanticDecision1, AtomicRule1, ReviewRoleRequirement1, ReviewPolicy1 and EvidenceRequirement1 use 1.0; EvidenceContract2 and ControlDefinition2 use 2.0. They do not change the frozen manifest. The new original-component reader retains existing control, numeric evidence, authority, freshness, adapter and reviewer identity-policy bytes and owning digests. An adapter's reference-only format binding does not add a schema field to the original wire. LegacyControlBinding1 is separately version-pinned provisional at 1.0. Its bounded original-pack reader retains the complete original StandardPackV2 2.0 wire and signature; the membership relation does not migrate legacy controls. InvalidatorObservation1, FreshnessProof1 and the independent evidence-subject preimage are separately version-pinned provisional at 1.0; EvidenceReference2 is provisional at 2.0. Their actual original owner proofs and freshness policies keep their existing wire versions. The original numeric evidence reference and assessment consumers remain unchanged.

PolicyHold1 is separately version-pinned provisional at 1.0. Its exact seven-field declaration preserves bounded hold provenance; parsing does not authenticate applicability, clear a hold or admit a selected policy.

ExtractorRegistryV3 and EffectOperationsV3 are separately version-pinned provisional at 3.0. Their complete candidate metadata does not add a supported effect handler or change original v2 catalogues, digests or selected consumers.

QualityProjectionRowV3 is separately version-pinned provisional at 3.0. Its original and qualitative cases preserve their actual control generations; complete row/control binding does not select a lock or authenticate decisions. SelectedControlAssessment2 is separately version-pinned provisional at 2.0. Its original evidence reference binding 1.0 adds no legacy schema header; review-attestation references keep schema 2.0, the original complete owning digest and the unchanged rigor-foundry.reviewer-attestation.v1 domain.

docs.title: Compatibility rules
docs.text:
• A published schema identifier is never reinterpreted. An incompatible wire change requires a new identifier, an explicit migration, and a retained old reader for the supported major line.
  • Stable Python names and CLI spellings are not removed or incompatibly rebound within the 1.x line.
  • A stable surface must remain available while deprecated. Removal within the same major line requires at least two intervening minor releases; an explicit new major may remove it.
  • Additive CLI options, commands, schemas, and stable Python names still require an intentional contract update and compatibility review. They are not admitted by parser drift.
  • Provisional Python imports require an explicit changelog entry before an incompatible change. Consumers should pin the package and the relevant schema rather than infer stability from importability.

There are no deprecated stable Python imports or CLI commands in the frozen 1.0 contract.

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
Compatibility is not correctness, legal conformity, or operational authority. The contract does not turn a candidate into a defect verdict, make CRA evidence an authority submission, authorise remediation or fleet activation, or make an unavailable dependency pass. Schema compatibility also does not override signature, digest, freshness, trust-policy, or exact-Git-object checks.

The contract intentionally says nothing about GitHub-hosted runner image or setup-python artifact provenance beyond the repository's existing pins. That external residual remains separately tracked and cannot be closed by a local manifest.

docs.title: Supply-chain rules
docs.text: Rule-pack rigor-foundry/1.9.0 adds a bounded supply-chain category (prefix SC) of high-precision rules over tracked Python requirement files. Like every RigorFoundry rule, each SC finding is an anchored needs-evidence candidate, never a verdict: it marks a real dependency-integrity surface for review, not a proven compromise. The rules are deliberately narrow to keep false positives low; breadth is not an acceptance metric.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rule Signal Confidence SC001-unhashed-pinned-requirement a pinned (==) requirement in a hash-mode lock file that carries no --hash= digest high SC002-vcs-url-requirement a dependency installed from a VCS checkout (git+, hg+, svn+, bzr+) or a PEP 508 direct URL (name @ https://…) high

SC001 activates only for a requirement file that already demonstrates hash mode — at least one line carries a --hash= digest — and then flags any pinned requirement in that file with no accompanying hash. Such a gap means the artefact is installed without verification against tampering or index substitution. It is near-zero false-positive by construction: pip-compile --generate-hashes output hashes every entry, so a missing hash is a genuine integrity hole and not a stylistic choice. SC002 flags a dependency resolved outside the package index and its recorded hashes — a mutable, unverified artefact.

Both rules parse requirement lines, joining backslash-continued blocks, and skip comments and index-configuration options: --index-url https://…, --extra-index-url, and --find-links are configuration, not dependencies, and are not flagged. Scope is limited to files named requirements*.txt / requirements*.in or any .txt / .in file under a requirements/ directory; .in source inputs are never subject to SC001 because they carry no hashes by design, but a VCS or URL dependency in an .in is still a real SC002 concern.

Each candidate carries a repository-tree anchor (path, line, content SHA-256), a neutral rationale, and a concrete verification procedure — for SC001, recompile the lock with --generate-hashes so every pin carries a digest; for SC002, pin the dependency to an immutable released version from the index with a recorded hash, or vendor and audit the exact revision if a direct source is genuinely required.

docs.title: Precision and applicability
docs.text: The rules match on requirement structure, not on arbitrary text, so a URL inside a comment or a non-requirements file is not flagged, and a fully hashed lock produces no candidate. The category contributes a portable control toward the supply-chain audit domain over the tracked requirement surface, so a repository that declares that domain required is now covered by a portable rule as well as any wired native adapter (for example a Trivy or Grype profile).

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text: False-positive calibration against real repositories is deliberately separate work: these rules ship with safe-and-vulnerable fixtures and precise requirement parsing, but adjudicated false-positive and reviewer-effort evidence across adopter repositories is the maturity-lifecycle step that promotes a rule from candidate breadth to calibrated enforcement.

docs.title: Task contexts and original remediation sources
docs.text: The provisional module APIs join the complete maintained inventory and source facts to an explicit general task and declared event. Their fixed source composer revalidates the actual original task/registry/inventory entries and optional retained remediation files. The result verifies source identity; an enclosing host must authenticate the initiating user, event, claim and audit request before deciding whether an operation is allowed.

docs.title: Complete task data
docs.text:
task_context.TaskContext1 uses schema 1.0 and object kind task-context. It contains the original general task reference and task proof, actor, project, owning group, root, registry generation/digest, task lifecycle, declared event, full maintained inventory, fact context, nullable claim proof and remediation binding, independent task identity and final context digest.

The independent task identity hashes only schema 1.0, object kind task-identity, task ID/definition, actor, project, group and root. It precedes the task proof, facts and final context, so no enclosing hash becomes its own input subject. Original task, registry and full inventory facts must agree with these fields. The context requires one registry observation identity and distinct task/registry/inventory owners, exact proof membership and every known mandatory source domain. Matching labels alone cannot authenticate a source.

Accepted declared events are claim, start, scope-change, dependency-change, mutation, verification, review, commit, publication, process, closure and audit. These are data labels. A publication context does not grant publication authority.

build, from_dict and direct immutable instances enforce the same closed field/version/relationship contract. The explicit parser budget bounds the aggregate nested roots, surfaces, proofs, observations and array values before nested model allocation. Direct instances also obey the hard reference ceiling. Parsing verifies data integrity and relationships; actual source verification remains required.

docs.title: Original remediation records
docs.text:
General work uses a real TaskDefinition1 without inventing an audit report or review. A task explicitly connected to an existing remediation can additionally carry remediation_task_binding.RemediationTaskBinding1: the original work-task reference, nullable complete record and closure references, and its binding digest. A closure requires its original complete record; all references name the same original task.

work_context_sources supplies fixed adapters for the existing WorkTask, WorkRecord and WorkClosure models. Existing task and closure source bytes retain their original schema 1.0 and definition/closure digests. Their public owning parsers remain responsible for validation.

The original WorkRecord has no public wire serializer or complete record digest. WorkRecordSource1 therefore owns an explicit retained-source projection with exactly schema_version, object_kind=work-record, the original task mapping and complete events array. Its reference digest binds that entire projection, including the task definition; the latest event digest alone is insufficient. This adapter preserves original WorkRecord.build semantics and exposes the same serialisation/reference interface as other retained sources. Its parser limits are held separately from source identity.

Fixed source kind/version Actual parser and identity work-task / 1.0 Original WorkTask.from_dict; original definition digest work-record / 1.0 Complete WorkRecordSource1 projection rebuilt through original task/event parsers and WorkRecord.build; full projection digest work-closure / 1.0 Original WorkClosure.from_dict; original closure digest

Unknown pairs refuse before lookup. These kinds are available through the existing fixed parse_context_source_target and RetainedContextSource interfaces. Data never chooses a loader, callback, path or executable.

RemediationSources borrows actual retained task, optional record and optional closure selections. observe(budget=...) reads and revalidates their fixed types, complete task-definition equality and original event/closure binding, then repeats the original source reads. The host keeps the leases open through the enclosing task consumer and closes them afterward. No source is closed or replaced by the binding API.

docs.title: Actual source composition
docs.text:
source_task_context.observe_source_task_context accepts exact installed TaskRegistrySourceOwners and InventorySourceOwner entries, the original actor/root, declared event and explicit budget. Optional RemediationSources must be actual borrowed entries. It derives current complete source facts, independently observes the task and inventory, builds the context and verifies the original owners before returning.

verify_source_task_context rebuilds the complete context from those actual entries and the separately supplied declared event. Another owning entry, changed source or different declared event cannot reuse earlier context data. The composer emits a null claim proof. Caller-supplied claim metadata cannot become an authenticated claim by passing through this source-only entry.

evaluate_source_task_condition verifies the whole context before and after calling the original three-valued condition evaluator. It returns ConditionTruth.TRUE, FALSE or UNKNOWN; Boolean coercion remains forbidden. Missing exact facts stay unknown, invalid known operands refuse, and no decisive sibling excuses an incomplete maintained inventory.

These APIs do not select a policy generation, authenticate initiating authority, verify a live claim, admit a root or execute an effect. Selected policy still owns which events require a claim and every other admission obligation. Package-root exports and the installed CLI retain their existing contracts.

docs.title: Task and registry source owners
docs.text: task_registry_source_owners.TaskRegistrySourceOwners derives observations from the actual retained general task definition, original project registry and two producer contracts. It provides fixed task and registry readers for host composition. All four source selections and the implementation snapshot come from the host; this API has no wire constructor or provider loader.

docs.title: Select and retain inputs
docs.text:
Use RetainedContextSource for each of the four source files. Before opening the owner selection, obtain an implementation snapshot with context_owner_implementation.observe_owner_implementation(package_root, budget=budget), where the host selects the installed package directory.

The observer includes every regular package file, including nested modules and runtime data, plus the bytes of the actual Python interpreter and its runtime identity. It excludes generated __pycache__ contents. Symlinks, nonregular entries, hardlinked files, missing package initializers, changing object identities and exceeded source, byte or entry budgets refuse. Limits must explicitly accommodate the full package and interpreter.

The fixed owners independently observe their own package directory at each use and compare the complete snapshot with the host's selection. Supplying a snapshot of another directory or a different implementation does not appoint a reader. The implementation content digest must also match both actual producer contracts.

from rigor_foundry.task_registry_source_owners import TaskRegistrySourceOwners
